body.text: Kāśyapaparivarta Sūtra
body.translated_text: <s>Kāśyapaparivarta Sūtra</s> (The Chapter on <s>Kāśyapa</s>)

body.text: siddham evaṃ mayā śrutamekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / gṛddhakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena sārddham aṣṭābhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ ṣodaśabhiśca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ nānābuddhakṣetrasannipatitairekajātiprabaddhairyadutānutarasyāṃ samyaksambodhau /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛddhakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) — eight thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> and sixteen thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, assembled from various <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), bound to one birth, that is, to unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: KP.1 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapam āmantrayati sma / katame catvāraḥ yaduta agauravau bhavati dharme ca dharmabhāṇake ca / dharma ...... ca bhavanti / dharmācāryamuṣṭiñca karoti dharmakāmānañca pudgalānāṃ dharmāntarāyaṃ karauti vicchanda ..... vikṣipati / na deśayati / praticchādayati / ābhimāntikaśca bhavatyātmotkarṣī parapaṃsakaḥ / ime kāśyapa catvāro dharma bodhisattvasya prajñāpārihāṇāya saṃvartate / tatredam ucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.1 There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: What are the four [dharmas]? Namely, one is disrespectful toward the <s>Dharma</s> and toward the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma); [...] and they become [...]; one withholds the <s>Dharma</s> like a teacher's closed fist; and one creates obstacles to the <s>Dharma</s> for persons who desire the <s>Dharma</s>, disrupting [...] and casting away; one does not teach; one conceals [the teaching]; and one is arrogant, self-exalting, and disparaging of others. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that lead to the decline of a <s>bodhisattva's</s> <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
agauravo bhavati ca dharmabhāṇake /
dharmeṣu mātsaryarato ca bhoti /
ācāryamuṣṭiñccha karoti dharme
dharmārthi kānā ca karoti vighnam
vicchadayanto vividhaṃ kṣipanto
dharmaṃ na deśayati jinapraśastān
so ātmotkarṣaṇi nittyayukto
parapaṃsane cābhirataḥ kusidau /
caturo ime dharmā jinena proktā
prajñāprahāṇāya jinorsānām
etāṃ hi catvāri jahitvā dharmāś
caturau parāṃ dharma jinokta bhāvayet

KP.2 catvārā ime kāśyapa dharmā bodhisattvasya mahāprajñātāyaiḥ saṃvartante / katame catvāraḥ yadu sagauravo bhavati dharme ca dharmabhāṇake ca / yathāśrutāṃśca dharmān yathāparyāptān parebhyo vistareṇa samprakāśayati / nirāmiṣeṇa cittenāpratikāṅkṣayati ..........
body.translated_text: KP.2 These are the four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that lead to a <s>bodhisattva's</s> great wisdom. What are the four? Namely, one is respectful toward the <s>Dharma</s> and toward the <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma); and one illuminates the <s>dharmas</s> as heard and as understood to others in detail, with a mind free from material gain, without expectation [...]

body.text: KP.3 .................... ca sattvānām avarṇāyaśaṃ kīrrtiśabdaślokaniścāraṇatayā / māyāśāṭṭhyena ca param upacarati nādhyāśaye na / ebhiḥ kāśyapa caturbhiḥ dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhicittaṃ muhyati / vāṃ tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.3 [...] and [one engages in] spreading ill-repute, infamy, and bad report regarding beings; and one approaches others with deceit and fraud, not with sincere intention. By these four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) of one who possesses [them] becomes confused. Regarding this, it is said:

KP.4 caturbhiḥ kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhisattvasya / sarvāsu jātiṣu jatamātrasya bodhicittam āmukhī bhavati na cāntarā ..... hyati yāvad bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanāt / katamaiścaturbhiḥ yaduta jīvitahetorapi samprajāna mṛṣāvādaṃ na bhāṣate / antamaśa hāsyaprekṣyam api / adhyāśayena sarvasattvānām antike tiṣṭhatyapagatamāyāśāṭṭhyatayā / sarvabodhisattveṣu ca śāstṛsañjñām utpādayati / caturdiśāṃ ....... cārayati / yāśca sattvān paripācayati tān , sarvān uttarasyāṃ samyaksambodhau samādāpaya ....... kayānaspṛhaṇatayā / ebhiḥ kāśyapa caturbhiḥ dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhisattvasya sarvāsu jātiṣu jātamātrasya bodhicittam āmukhibhavati na cāntarā muhyati yāvad bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanāt / tatredamucyate // 4 //
body.translated_text: KP.4 By four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses them — in all births, as soon as born, the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) becomes manifest and does not become confused in between, until sitting at the seat of awakening. By which four? Namely, one does not speak a deliberate lie even for the sake of one's life, not even in jest; one stands before all beings with sincere intention, free from deceit and fraud; one generates the perception of a teacher toward all <s>bodhisattvas</s>; and one spreads [their fame] in the four directions [...]; and whatever beings one matures, one establishes all of them in unsurpassed perfect awakening [...] without craving. By these four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses them — in all births, as soon as born, the <s>bodhicitta</s> becomes manifest and does not become confused in between, until sitting at the seat of awakening. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
na jivitārthe anṛtaṃ vadanti
bhāṣanti vācaṃ sadā arthayuktaṃ /
māyāya śaṭṭhye ..... tya varjitā
adhyāśayena sadā sattva paśyati /
bodhāya ye prasthita śuddhasattvā
śāsteti tān manyati bodhisa(ttva) ....
varṇaṃ ca teṣāṃ bhaṇate caturdiśaṃ
śāstāra sañjñāṃ sadupasthapitvā 2
yāṃścāpi sattvān paripācayati

children.text: annuttare jñāne samādapeti
children.translated_text: and whatever beings one matures, one establishes them in the unsurpassed knowledge;

children.text: eteṣu dharmeṣu pratiṣṭhitānāṃ
children.translated_text: for those established in these <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: cittaṃ na bodhāya kadāci muhyatiḥ 3 //
children.translated_text: the mind never becomes confused regarding awakening.

body.text: KP.5 caturbhiḥ kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhisattvasyotpannotpannāma kuśalā dharmāḥ paryādīyante yairna vivardhanti ... rdharmaiḥ katamaiścaturbhiḥ yaduta abhimānikasya lokāyatanamantraparyeṣṭyā / aśrutānām anuddiṣṭānām ca sū ....... ṇa ebhiḥ kāśyapa caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya bodhisattvasyotpannotpannā kuśalān dha ..... vivardhate kuśalairdharmaiḥ tatredamucyate // 5 //
body.translated_text: KP.5 By four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses them, as they arise, are diminished and do not increase. By which four? Namely, seeking worldly philosophy (<s>lokāyata</s>) and mantras out of arrogance; and [...] sūtras that have not been heard or taught [...]. By these four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses them, as they arise, do not increase in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
lokāyikam eṣati ābhimāniko
kulāni ........
buddhaurasā dviṣate ca bodhisattvāṃs
teṣām avarṇaṃ bhaṇate samantāt /
noddiṣṭato cāpi śrutā ...
... kṣipitā imi jinena proktāt /
tamehi dharmehi samanvitasya
kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu na vṛddhirasti /
tasmād ..... ta bodhisattvo
durān vijahyāccaturo pi dharmān /
imā niṣevanta sudūri bodhaye
nabhaṃ va bhūmīya sudūradūraṃ .....

KP.6 caturbhiḥ kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ aparihāṇadharmā bhavati viśeṣagāmitayai katamaiścaturbhiḥ suśrutaṃ paryeṣṭi na duśrutaṃ / yaduta ṣaṭpāramitābodhisattvapiṭakaparyeṣt śvasadṛśaśca bhavati nirmāṇatayā sarvasattveṣu dharmalābhasantuṣṭa ca bhavati / sarvamithyājīvaparivarjitaḥ āryavaṃśasantuṣṭ..... tāya cāpatyā na parāṃścodayati / na ca dośāntaraskhalitagaveṣī bhavati / yeṣcāsya buddhirna gāhate tatra tathāgatam eva sākṣīti kṛtvā na pratikṣipati // tathāgata eva jānāti nāhaṃ ........dhirnānādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ yathādhimuktikatayā dharmadeśanā pravartate / ebhiḥ kāśyapa caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ aparihāṇadharma bhavati viśeṣagamitāyai / tatredamucyate // 6 //
body.translated_text: KP.6 By four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses them becomes one of non-declining nature, progressing toward distinction. By which four? One seeks what is well-heard, not what is ill-heard — namely, seeking the <s>ṣaṭpāramitā</s> (six perfections) and the <s>bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> (bodhisattva collection); and one becomes like a dog in humility toward all beings; and one is content with the gain of <s>Dharma</s>; having abandoned all wrong livelihood, content with the <s>āryavaṃśa</s> (noble lineage) [...]; one does not accuse others of offenses, and one does not seek others' faults and stumbles; and regarding what one's intellect does not grasp, one takes the <s>Tathāgata</s> as witness and does not reject it, [thinking:] 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> alone knows, not I [...] the <s>Dharma</s> teaching proceeds according to the dispositions of beings of various inclinations.' By these four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses them becomes one of non-declining nature, progressing toward distinction. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
nityaṃ ca so.. yukto
upāyakauśalyatha bodhipīṭake //
body.translated_text:
And one is always engaged [...]
in skillful means and the <s>bodhipiṭaka</s> (awakening collection).

children.text: imā tu dharmāścaturo viditvā
children.translated_text: Having understood these four <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text: KP.7 catvāra ime kāśyapa kuṭilāścittotpādāstena bodhisattvena parivarjitavyāḥ katameścatvāraryaduta kāṅkṣā vimatirvicikitsā sarvabuddhadharmeṣu / mānamadamrakṣakrodhavyāpādāḥ sarvasattveṣu irṣyāmātsaryaṃ paralābheṣu avarṇāyaśokīrtiśabdaślokaniścāraṇatayā...... ime kāśyapa catvāraḥ kuṭilāścittotpādāste bodhisattvena parivarjitavyāḥ tatredamucyate // 7 //
body.translated_text: KP.7 These are the four crooked mental attitudes, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that should be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Which four? Namely, doubt, uncertainty, and hesitation regarding all <s>buddhadharmas</s> (Buddha-qualities); pride, intoxication, arrogance, anger, and malice toward all beings; jealousy and envy regarding others' gains; spreading ill-repute, infamy, and bad report [...]. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four crooked mental attitudes that should be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
dharmeṣu kāṅkṣāṃ vimatiṃ ca kurvati
sattveṣu mānam atha krodhaṃ sevati /
mātsaryam irṣyā paralābha kurvate
jine prasādaṃ ca na ........

children.text: akīrtyavarṇam ayaśaṃ ca cārayī
children.translated_text: one who spreads infamy, ill-repute, and dishonor

children.text: so bodhisattveṣu sadā avidvāt /
children.translated_text: toward the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, always being ignorant;

children.text: catvāri cittā kuṭilā vivarjaye ......
children.translated_text: these four crooked mental attitudes should be abandoned [...]

children.text: ...... pakṣaṃ sadā bodhisattvaḥ 2 //
children.translated_text: [...] always taking the side of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.translated_text:
One who harbors doubt and uncertainty regarding the <s>dharmas</s>,
who cultivates pride and anger toward beings,
who harbors jealousy and envy regarding others' gains,
and has no faith in the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) [...]

body.text: KP.8 catvāra ime kāśyapa ṛjukasya bodhisattvasya ṛjukalakṣaṇāni bhavanti katamāni catvāriryaduta āpattiāpanno na pracchādāyatācaṣṭe vivṛṇoti niṣparyutthāno bhavati / yena satyavacanena rājapārihāṇirvā dhanāpārihāṇirvā kāyajīvitāntarāyo bhavet tat satyavacanaṃ na vigūhati nānyenānyaṃ prati nisṛtya vācā bhāṣate / sarvaparopakrameṣu cākrośaparibhāṣaṇakuṃsanapaṃsantāḍana tarjanavadhabandhanāparādheṣvātmāparādhī bhavati / karmavipākapratisaraṇo na pareṣāṃ kupyati nā nuśayaṃ vahati / sa śraddhāpratiṣṭhitaśca bhavati / sarvāśraddheyānapi buddhadharmā śraddadhāti āśayaśuddhatām upādāya / ime kāśyapa catvāro ṛjukasya bodhisattvasya ṛjukalakṣaṇāni bhavanti / tatredamucyate // 8 //
body.translated_text: KP.8 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four characteristics of straightforwardness (<s>ṛjukalakṣaṇa</s>) of a straightforward <s>bodhisattva</s>. What are the four? When one has committed a transgression, one does not conceal it but confesses and reveals it, and becomes free from remorse. One does not hide truthful speech even when that truthful speech would result in the loss of royal [favor], or the loss of wealth, or danger to one's body and life. One does not speak deceitful words to one person about another. And in all hostile encounters — abuse, reviling, reproach, slander, beating, threatening, violence, and imprisonment — one considers oneself at fault. One relies on the ripening of <s>karma</s> and does not become angry at others nor harbor resentment. And one is established in faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). One has faith even in all the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities that are beyond [ordinary] belief, by virtue of purity of intention. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four characteristics of straightforwardness of a straightforward <s>bodhisattva</s>. Herein it is said: // 8 //

children.translated_text: These characteristics of straightforwardness have been declared by the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror);

body.translated_text: When they have committed a transgression, they do not conceal it; they confess and reveal it, and are free from fault. For the sake of wealth, kingship, or life [lacuna], they speak what is true and impart instruction. In abuse, reproach, and slander, in beatings, imprisonments, and confinements, one considers oneself at fault and is not angry at others, bearing one's own <s>karma</s> and not harboring resentment. 2. One has faith in the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones),

body.text: KP.9 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattva khaḍuṅkāḥ katame catvāraḥ śrutoddhatadharmavihārī ca bhavati na ca pratipadyate / dharmānudharmapratipattim anuśāsane nuddhatadharmavihārī ca bhavati / na ca śuśrūṣatyācāryopādhyāyānāṃ / śraddhādeyaṃ vinipātayati cyuta pratijñaśca śraddhādeyāṃ paribhuṅkte / dāntājāneyaprāpitāṃśca bodhisattvāṃ dṛṣṭvā agoravo bhavati mānagrāhī / ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvākhaḍuṅkāḥ tatredamucyate // 9 //
body.translated_text: KP.9 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four [types of] stubborn <s>bodhisattvas</s> (<s>khaḍuṅka</s>). What are the four? One who dwells in the <s>Dharma</s> with arrogance born of learning, yet does not practice the practice conforming to the <s>Dharma</s> in accordance with the teaching. One who is not arrogant in dwelling in the <s>Dharma</s>, yet does not listen respectfully to one's teachers and preceptors. One who squanders what was given in faith, having fallen from one's vows, and consumes the gifts given in faith. And one who, upon seeing <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the state of being tamed and noble, shows no respect and is seized by pride. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four [types of] stubborn <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Herein it is said: // 9 //

body.text:
śrutena oddhatyavihāri bhoti na coddhato gacchati ānuśāsaniṃ /
so uddhato sevati sarvadharmān śuśrūṣate na ca āryāṃ kathañcit /
cyutapratijño paribhuñjate sadā śraddhāya dinnāni subhojanāni /

children.text: ājanyaprāptānapi bodhisattvān paśyitvā no gauravatā karoti / 2
children.translated_text: And upon seeing <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained noble stature, one does not show respect. 2

children.text:
mānaṃ ca so bṛṃhayate khaḍuṅko nirmāṇa to sevati bodhisattvān
ete khaḍuṅkā sugatena proktā jīnātmajāste parivarjanīyāt 3 //
children.translated_text: That stubborn one (<s>khaḍuṅka</s>) nourishes pride and resorts to <s>bodhisattvas</s> with contempt. These stubborn ones have been declared by the <s>Sugata</s>; they, the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, should be avoided. 3 //

body.translated_text: One who dwells with arrogance from learning, yet the arrogant one does not follow the teaching; that arrogant one resorts to all [manner of] practices yet does not in any way listen respectfully to the noble ones. Having fallen from one's vows, one always consumes the excellent foods given in faith.

body.text: KP.10 catvāra ime kāśyapa ājāneyā bodhisattvāḥ katame catvāraḥ suśrutaṃ śruṇoti tatra ca pratipadyate / arthapratisaraṇaśca bhavati na vyañjanapratisaraṇaḥ pradakṣiṇagrāhī bhavatyavavādānuśāsane / suvacaḥ sukṛtakarmakārī ca bhavati / guruśuśrūṣaniryātaḥ ājāneyabhojanāni ca paribhūṅkte / acyutaśīlasamādhirdāntājāneyaprāptaśca bodhisattvāṃ dṛṣṭvā sagauravo bhavati sapratīśaḥ tannimnaḥ tatpravaṇaḥ tatprāgbhāraḥ tadguṇapratikāṅkṣī / ime kāśyapa catvāro ājāneyā bodhisattvā tatredam ucyate 10 //
body.translated_text: KP.10 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four [types of] noble <s>bodhisattvas</s> (<s>ājāneya</s>). What are the four? One who hears what is well-learned and practices accordingly. One who relies on meaning, not on the letter, and who receives admonition and instruction with compliance. One who is tractable and a doer of well-performed deeds. One who has set forth in respectful service to teachers and partakes of the sustenance of the noble. One whose moral conduct and concentration are unshaken, and who, upon seeing <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the state of being tamed and noble, shows respect, is reverential, is inclined toward them, tends toward them, gravitates toward them, and aspires to their virtues. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four [types of] noble <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Herein it is said: 10 //

body.text:
śruṇoti yaṃ suśrutataṃ karoti
dharmārthasāro pratipattisusthitaḥ
pradakṣiṇaṃ gṛhṇati ānuśāsanīṃ
suvaco guru sevati dharmakāma /
śīle samādhau ca sadā pratiṣṭhito /
subhojanaṃ bhuñjati śīlasaṃvṛtaḥ
sagauravo bhavati ca sapradeśo
tannimna tatproṇu guṇābhikāṅkṣi 2

children.text: ājanyaprāptāśca jinorasā ye
children.translated_text: And those who have attained noble stature, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> —

children.text: premeṇa tāṃ paśyati nityakālam /
children.translated_text: one regards them with love at all times.

children.text: catvāra etan sugato X diṣṭā
children.translated_text: These four have been declared by the <s>Sugata</s>:

children.text: ājanyaprāptā sugatasya putrāḥ 3 //
children.translated_text: those who have attained noble stature, the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>. 3 //

body.translated_text: One hears what is well-learned and acts upon it; firmly established in practice, with the essence of the <s>Dharma</s>'s meaning. One receives instruction with compliance, is tractable, serves the teacher, and desires the <s>Dharma</s>. Always established in moral conduct and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), one partakes of excellent food while restrained in conduct. One is respectful and reverential, inclined toward them and tending toward them, aspiring to their virtues. 2

body.text: KP.11 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisatvaskhalitāni / katamāni catvāri aparipāciteṣu satveṣu viśvāso bodhisattvasya skhalitaṃ / abhājanībhūte sattveṣūdārabuddhadharmasamprakāśanatā bodhisattvasya skhalitam udārādhimuktikeṣu sattveṣu hīnayānasamprakāśanā bodhisattvasya skhalitaṃ samyakpratyupasthiteṣu sattveṣu śīlavatsu kalyāṇadharmaprati mānanā duḥśīlapāpadharmasaṅgraho bodhisattvasya skhali X imā kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvaskhalitāni / tatredamucyate // 10 //
body.translated_text: KP.11 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four stumbling blocks (<s>skhalita</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. What are the four? Trust in beings who have not been matured is a stumbling block for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Displaying the exalted <s>Buddha</s>-qualities to beings who are unfit vessels is a stumbling block for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Displaying the lesser vehicle (<s>hīnayāna</s>) to beings of exalted aspiration is a stumbling block for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Despising those of virtuous character who are rightly established, beings endowed with wholesome qualities, and instead gathering those of bad conduct and evil qualities — this is a stumbling block for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four stumbling blocks of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Herein it is said: // 10 //

body.text:
na viśvaseyāparipāciteṣu abhājane dharma udāra no bhaṇe /
udāradharmeṣu na hīnayāne prakāśaye jātu sa bodhisattvo /
samyaksthitāṃ śīlaguṇopapetān kalyāṇadharmā na vimānayeta /

children.text: duḥśīlasattvā na parigraheyā pāpaṃ ca dharmān parivarjayetaḥ
children.translated_text: Beings of bad conduct should not be embraced, and evil qualities should be abandoned.

children.text: skhalitāni catvāri imāni jñātvā vivarjayeddūrata bodhisattvāḥ
children.translated_text: Having understood these four stumbling blocks, <s>bodhisattvas</s> should avoid them from afar.

children.text: imā niṣevaṃ tu na bodhi buddhyate tasmād vivarjed imi dharma paṇḍitaḥ 3 //
children.translated_text: One who resorts to these does not attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening); therefore the wise one should avoid these practices. 3 //

body.translated_text: One should not trust those who have not been matured; one should not teach the exalted <s>Dharma</s> to the unfit vessel. One should never display the lesser vehicle to those of exalted <s>Dharma</s> — so should a <s>bodhisattva</s> [act]. One should not despise those who are rightly established, endowed with virtuous qualities and wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.12 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvamārgāḥ katame catvāraḥ samacittatā sarvasattveṣu / buddhajñānasamādāpanatā sarvasattveṣu samadharmadeśanā sarvasattveṣu samyakprayogatā sarvasattveṣu / 4 ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvamārgāḥ tatredam idamucyate 12 //
body.translated_text: KP.12 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four paths of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. What are the four? Equanimity of mind toward all beings. Encouraging all beings toward the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>. Equal teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings. Right effort toward all beings. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four paths of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Herein it is said: 12 //

children.text: samacitta sattveṣu bhata nityaṃ samādapeyādiha buddhayāne /
children.translated_text: One should always maintain equanimity of mind toward beings; one should encourage them in the <s>Buddha</s>-vehicle here.

children.text: dharmāṃ ca deśetā jinapraśastaṃ sarveṣu sattveṣu prasannacitto /
children.translated_text: One should teach the <s>Dharma</s> praised by the <s>Jina</s>, with a serene mind toward all beings.

children.text: samyakprayuktā pratipattisusthito sarveṣu sattveṣu samaṃ careta /
children.translated_text: Rightly exerting oneself, firmly established in practice, one should conduct oneself equally toward all beings.

children.text: mārgān imāṃścatura jinapraśastāṃ jinorasā sada taṃ bhāvayanti // 3 //
children.translated_text: These four paths praised by the <s>Jina</s>, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> always cultivate them. // 3 //

body.text: KP.13 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvasya kumitrāṇi kusahāyāste bodhisattvena parivarjayitavyā / katamāni catvāri / śrāvakayānīyo bhikṣu ātmahitāya pratipannaḥ pratyekabuddhayānīyo 'lpārtho 'lpakṛtyaḥ lokāyatiko vicitramantrapratibhānaḥ yaṃ ca pudgalaṃ sevamāna tato lokāmiṣasaṅgraho bhavati na dharmasaṅgrahaḥ ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvasya kumitrāṇi kusahāyās te bodhisattvena parivarjayitavyāḥ tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.13 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four bad friends and bad companions (<s>kumitra</s>, <s>kusahāya</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, and they should be avoided by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. What are the four? A monk inclined to the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle who is intent on his own benefit. A follower of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle who is of little purpose and little activity. A follower of <s>Lokāyata</s> (worldly materialism) skilled in various clever mantras. And whatever person, when associated with, leads to the accumulation of worldly gains rather than the accumulation of <s>Dharma</s>. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four bad friends and bad companions of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, and they should be avoided by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Herein it is said: //

body.text:
ye śrāvakā ātmahitāya yuktā yogaṃ ca ye pravrajitāścaranti /
pratyekabuddhāpi ca ye 'lpakṛtyā alpārthasaṃsargā vivarjayanti /
lokāyataṃ ye ca paḥhanti bālā vigrāhikā yatra kathopadiṣṭā /
yaṃ sevamānāmiṣasaṅgraho bhaved bhaven na dharmasya ca saṅgraho yahim 2 /
tān bodhisattvāścaturo prahāya kalyāṇamitrāścaturo bhajanti /

children.text: ete kumitrā kusahāyayuktā jinena dūrāt parivarjanīyā / 3 //
children.translated_text: These are bad friends joined with bad companions; by the <s>Jina</s>'s [teaching], they should be avoided from afar. 3 //

body.translated_text: Those <s>Śrāvakas</s> who are devoted to their own benefit, and those renunciants who pursue [their own] spiritual practice; and the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who are of little activity, who avoid association with those of little purpose; and the foolish ones who study <s>Lokāyata</s>, where contentious disputations are taught; and whoever, when associated with, leads to the accumulation of worldly gains but not to the accumulation of <s>Dharma</s>. 2 A <s>bodhisattva</s>, having abandoned those four, should resort to four [types of] good friends.

body.text: KP.14 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvasya bhūtakalyāṇamitrāṇi / katamāni catvāri / yācanako bodhisattvasya bhūtakalyāṇamitraṃ bodhimārgopastambhāya saṃvartate dharmabhāṇako bodhisattvasya bhūtakalyāṇamitraṃ śrutaprajñopastambhāya saṃvartate / pravrajyāsamādapako bodhisattvasya bhūtakalyāṇamitra sarvakuśalamūlopastambhāya / saṃvartate / buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvasya bhūtakalyāṇamitra sarvabuddhadharmopastambhāya saṃvartate / ime kāśyapa bodhisattvasya bhūtakalyāṇamitrāṇi tatredamucyate // 12 //
body.translated_text: KP.14 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four true good friends (<s>bhūtakalyāṇamitra</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. What are the four? One who asks [for gifts] is a true good friend of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, serving as a support for the path to awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>). A teacher of <s>Dharma</s> is a true good friend of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, serving as a support for the wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutaprajñā</s>). One who encourages renunciation (<s>pravrajyā</s>) is a true good friend of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, serving as a support for all roots of merit. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are the true good friends of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, serving as a support for all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the true good friends of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Herein it is said: // 12 //

body.text:
kalyāṇamitraṃ sa ca dāyakānāṃ pratigrāhako bodhiparigrahāya /
dharmārthavādī śrutaprajñakarī kalyāṇamitraṃ sugatena proktaṃ /
pravrajya ye cāpi samādapenti te mitramūlaṃ sugatasya vuktāḥ
buddhaśca mitraṃ sugatātmajānāṃ sambuddhamārgasyupastambhanāyaḥ
ete hi catvāri jinapraśastā kalyāṇamitrā sugatātmajānāṃ /

children.text: eta niṣeva X sadāpramantā prāpnoti bodhi sugatopadiṣṭā / 3 //
children.translated_text: Resorting to these, always diligent, one attains the <s>bodhi</s> taught by the <s>Sugata</s>. 3 //

body.translated_text: Among donors, the one who accepts [gifts] is a good friend, for the purpose of embracing <s>bodhi</s>. One who teaches the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>, producing the wisdom born of learning — that is declared a good friend by the <s>Sugata</s>. And those who encourage renunciation — they are called the root of friendship by the <s>Sugata</s>. And the <s>Buddha</s> is the friend of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, for the support of the path to full awakening (<s>sambuddhamārga</s>). These four, praised by the <s>Jina</s>, are the good friends of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.

body.text: KP.15 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvapratirūpa.... katame catvāra / lābhasatkārārthiko bhavati na dharmārthikāḥ kīrtiśabdaślokārthiko bhavati na guṇārthikaḥ ātmasukhārthiko bhavati na sattvaduḥkhā panayanārthikāḥ parṣadguṇārthiko bhavati na vivekārthikaḥ ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvapratirūpakāḥ tatredamucyate // 14 //
body.translated_text: KP.15 These are the four counterfeit <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s> [...]. What are the four? One who desires gain and honor, not the <s>Dharma</s>; one who desires fame and renown, not virtuous qualities; one who desires one's own happiness, not the removal of beings' suffering; one who desires a retinue's praise, not solitude. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four counterfeit <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: lābhārthiko bhavati na dharmakāmo kīrtyarthiko nneva guṇaibhirarthikaḥ

children.text: na sattvaduḥkhāpanayena cārthiko yo cātmano nitya sukh.....rthikaḥ
children.translated_text: one who does not seek to remove the suffering of beings, but always seeks one's own happiness;

children.text: parṣadguṇārthī na vivekakāmo sukhe prasakto na guṇeṣu sakto /
children.translated_text: one who desires a retinue's praise, not solitude; one attached to pleasure, not attached to virtuous qualities —

children.text: catvāra ete pratirūpakoktāḥ bodhisattvān parivarjanīyā 2 //
children.translated_text: these four are called counterfeit [<s>bodhisattvas</s>]; they should be avoided by the <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.translated_text: One who desires gain, not the <s>Dharma</s>; one who desires fame, not virtuous qualities;

body.text: KP.16 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvasya bhūtā bodhisattvaguṇā / katame catvāra śunyatāṃ cādhimucyate / karmavipākaṃ cābhiśraddadhāti / nairātmyaṃ cāsya kṣamate sarvasattveṣu mahākaruṇ. nirvāṇagataścāsyāśayaḥ saṃsāragataśca prayogaḥ sattvaparipākāya ca dānaṃ vipākāpratikāṅkṣanatā ca / ime kāśyapa catvāro dharmā bodhisattvasya bhūtā bodhisattvaguṇā tatredamucyate // 15 //
body.translated_text: KP.16 These are the four genuine <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. What are the four? One has faith in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and also has confidence in <s>karmavipāka</s> (the ripening of actions); one is patient with <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self) and generates great compassion toward all beings; one's intention is directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, yet one's effort is directed toward <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of maturing beings; and one gives gifts without expectation of their ripening. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that are the genuine <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: śunyāśca dharmān adhimucyate sadā vipāka pattīyati karmaṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: One always has faith in the <s>dharmas</s> as empty, and has confidence in the ripening of <s>karma</s>;

children.text: nairātmakṣāntyā samatāpratiṣṭhito karuṇāṃ ca sattveṣu janeti nityaṃ /
children.translated_text: established in equanimity through patience with <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self), one always generates compassion toward beings;

children.text: nirvāṇi bhāvo sata tasya bhoti prayoga saṃsāragataśca tasya /
children.translated_text: one's nature is inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, yet one's effort is directed toward <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: paripācanārthaṃ ca dadāti dānaṃ vipāka nākāṅkṣati karmaṇāṃ ca 2 //
children.translated_text: one gives gifts for the sake of maturing [beings], and does not expect the ripening of actions.

body.text:
KP.17 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvasya mahānidānapratilambhāḥ katame...........
buddhotpādārāgaṇatā / ṣaṭpāramitāśravaṇaḥ apratihatacittasya dharmabhāṇakadarśanaṃ / apramattasyāraṇyavāsābhirataḥ ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvasya mahānidhānapratilambhā / tatredamucyate / // 16 //
body.translated_text: KP.17 These are the four great treasure-attainments of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s> [...]. Delighting in the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>; hearing the <s>ṣaṭpāramitās</s> (six perfections); seeing a <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma) with an unobstructed mind; and for one who is diligent, delight in dwelling in the forest. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four great treasure-attainments of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
buddhānam ārāgaṇa sarvajātiṣu śravaśca ṣaṇṇāmapi pāramīṇām /
prasannacitto 'pi ca dharmabhāṇakāṃ sampaśyate gaurava jātu nityam /
sadāpramattasya cāraṇyavāso tatreva so bhoti ratiḥ sadāsya /

children.text: catvāra dharmā sugatena proktā mahānidhānāni jinātmajānām / 2 //
children.translated_text: these four <s>dharmas</s> are proclaimed by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) as the great treasures of the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror).

body.text:
KP.18 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvamārapathasamatikramaṇā dharmāḥ katame catvāraḥ bodhicittasyānutsargaḥ sarvasattveṣvapratihatacittatā /
sarvadṛṣṭīkṛtānām avabodhanā / anatimanyanā sarvasattveṣu ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvasya mārapathasamatikramaṇā dharmā / tatredamucyate // 17 //
body.translated_text: KP.18 These are the four <s>dharmas</s> for transcending <s>Māra's</s> path, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. What are the four? Not abandoning the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening); having an unobstructed mind toward all beings; awakening to [the nature of] all views that have been created; and not having contempt toward any beings. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> for the <s>bodhisattva</s> to transcend <s>Māra's</s> path. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: bodhāya cittaṃ na parityajanti sattveṣu ca pratigha jahanti nityam /

children.text: sarvāśca dṛṣṭigatanutsṛjaṃ... na cādhimanyanti ha sattvakāyam
children.translated_text: they let go of all views [...] and do not have contempt toward the assembly of beings;

children.text: catvāra ete sugatena proktā dharmā hi mārasya atikramāya
children.translated_text: these four are proclaimed by the <s>Sugata</s> as <s>dharmas</s> for transcending <s>Māra</s>;

children.text: ....... niṣevitva jinā bhavanti aṅgīrasā apratimā vināyakā 2 //
children.translated_text: [...] having cultivated these, they become <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, incomparable guides.

body.translated_text: They do not abandon the mind [set on] awakening, and they always relinquish hostility toward beings;

body.text: KP.19 catvāra ime kāśyapa dharmā bodhisattvasya sarvakuśa ladharmasaṅgrahāya saṃvartante / katame catvāraḥ niṣkuhakasyāraṇyavāsābhiratiḥ pratikārāprātikāṅkṣiṇaśc.......... saṅgrahavastūni sarvasattveṣu kāyajīvitotsargaḥ saddharmaparyeṣṭim ārabhyātṛptitā sarvakuśalamūlasamudānanāya / ime kāśyapa catvāro dharmā bodhisattvasya sarvakuśaladharmasaṅgrahāya saṃvartante tatredamucyate // 18 //
body.translated_text: KP.19 These are the four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that lead to the gathering of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. What are the four? For one free from deceit, delight in dwelling in the forest; practicing the <s>saṅgrahavastūni</s> (four means of gathering [disciples]) toward all beings without expectation of return [...]; sacrificing body and life; and insatiable pursuit of the true <s>Dharma</s>, beginning with the gathering of all wholesome roots. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that lead to the gathering of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: araṇyavāse kuhanāvivarjito sattveṣu ca saṅgraha yo jinoktā /

children.text: utsarga kāyasya ca jīvitasya saddharmaparyeṣṭi samārabhi.............
children.translated_text: sacrificing body and life, undertaking the pursuit of the true <s>Dharma</s> [...]

children.text: samudānanāyāśca sadā atṛpto kuśalāna mūlāna analpakānāṃ /
children.translated_text: and always insatiable in the gathering of the many, not insignificant, roots of wholesome [merit];

children.text: kuśalāna dharmāṇa ca saṅgrahārthe catvāro dharmā sugatena proktā 2 //
children.translated_text: for the gathering of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, these four <s>dharmas</s> are proclaimed by the <s>Sugata</s>.

body.translated_text: Free from deceit in forest dwelling, and practicing the means of gathering [disciples] toward beings as proclaimed by the <s>Jina</s>;

body.text: KP.20 catvāra ime kāśyapa bodhisattvasyāprameyā puṇyasambhārāḥ katame catvāraḥ nirāmiṣacittasyā dharmadānaṃ duḥśīleṣu ca sattveṣu mahākaruṇā sarvasattveṣu bodhicittārocanatā durbaleṣu sattveṣu kṣāntyā sevanatā / ime kāśyapa catvāro bodhisattvasyāprameyā puṇyasambhārāḥ tatredamucyate // 19 //
body.translated_text: KP.20 These are the four immeasurable accumulations of merit for a <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. What are the four? The gift of <s>Dharma</s> with a mind free from material gain; great compassion toward beings of bad moral conduct; encouraging the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) in all beings; and practicing patience toward weak beings. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four immeasurable accumulations of merit for a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Regarding this, it is said:
