children.translated_text: the merit of this cannot be counted.

body.translated_text:
The gift of <s>Dharma</s> praised by the <s>Jina</s>,
with a pure mind free from material gain;
intense compassion toward those of poor moral conduct;
and generating the mind [set on] awakening in others.
One practices patience toward the weak,
and [...] the gathering of <s>dharmas</s> [...] proclaimed.
Having cultivated these, they become <s>Jinas</s>;
these should always be cultivated by the <s>bodhisattvas</s>.
The eight sets of four should be abandoned [...],
those that create obstacles to awakening;
and the other twelve should be cultivated by the wise —
having touched the immortal, one attains awakening [...].
Those foremost beings who uphold, recite, and illuminate
this <s>Dharma</s>-guide —
the <s>Jina</s> declares their merit to be infinite;
[...] immeasurable, the <s>Jina</s> praises them.
Whoever would fill as many <s>kṣetras</s> (fields) as there are sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>
with jewels and give them away,
or whoever would recite a single four-line verse from this —

body.text: KP.21 catvāra ime kāśyapa dharmā bodhisattvasya avidyābhāgīyākleśasamati kramāya saṃvartante / katame catvāraḥ śīlasaṃvaraḥ saddharmaparigrahaḥ pradīpadānam antamaśaḥ saṃstutebhyaḥ ime kāśyapa catvāro dharmā bodhisattvasya avidyābhāgīyākleśasamatikramāya saṃvartante //
body.translated_text: KP.21 These are the four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that lead to the <s>bodhisattva's</s> transcendence of <s>avidyā</s>-related (ignorance-related) <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). What are the four? <s>Śīlasaṃvara</s> (moral restraint); embracing the true <s>Dharma</s>; offering of lamps; even from those who are [...] praised. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that lead to the <s>bodhisattva's</s> transcendence of ignorance-related afflictions.

body.text:
KP.22 catvāra ime kāśyapa dharmā bodhisattvasya anāvaraṇajñānatāye saṃvartante /
katame catvāraḥ yaduta indriyasaṃvaraḥ gambhīrārthavivaraṇatā svalābhenāvamanyanā / paralābhesvanadhya.......... natā / ime kāśyapa catvāro dharmā bodhisattvasyānāvaraṇajñānatāye saṃvartante / // 22 //
body.translated_text: KP.22 These are the four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that lead to the <s>bodhisattva's</s> attainment of unobstructed knowledge. What are the four? Namely, <s>indriyasaṃvara</s> (restraint of the sense faculties); elucidation of profound meanings; not being contemptuous of one's own gains; and not being [...] regarding others' gains. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that lead to the <s>bodhisattva's</s> attainment of unobstructed knowledge.

body.text: KP.23 na khalu kāśyapa nāmamātreṇa bodhisatvo mahāsattva ityucyate dharmacaryayā samacaryayā kuśalacaryayā dharm...... ritābhiḥ kāśyapa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate / dvātriṃśadbhi kāśyapa dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo ityucyate / katame dvātriṃśadbhiḥ yaduta hitasukhādhyāśayatayā sarvasattveṣu / sarvajñajñānāvatāraṇatayā kim ahammargāmīti pareṣāṃ jñānākunsanatā niradhimānatayā / dṛḍhādhyāśayatayā / akṛtrimaprematayā / atyantamitratā / mitrāmitreṣu samacittatayā / yāvannirvāṇaparyantatāye /
body.translated_text: KP.23 Indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not called so merely by name; one is called a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> by virtue of <s>Dharma</s>-practice, equanimous conduct, and wholesome conduct, endowed with <s>Dharma</s>-conduct [...], <s>Kāśyapa</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> is called so when endowed with thirty-two <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. What are the thirty-two? Namely: sincere intention for the benefit and happiness of all beings; descending into the knowledge of the omniscient; 'Am I a path-goer?' — not being contemptuous of others' knowledge, with humility; firm sincere intention; genuine and unfeigned affection; ultimate friendship; equal-mindedness toward friends and enemies alike; extending up to the limit of <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

body.text:
KP.24 anṛtavākyatā smitamukhapūrvābhibhāṣaṇatā nupādatteṣu bhāreṣv . v. ṣ. d.
n........... sarvasattveṣvaparicinnamahākaruṇatā aparikhinnamānasatayā saddharmaparyeṣṭim ārabhyātṛ....... śrutārthatayā / ātmaskhaliteṣu doṣadarśanātayā / paraskhalitesvaruṣṭāpatticodanatayā / sarvairyapatheṣu bodhicittaparikarmatayā / vipākāpratikāṅkṣiṇa tyāgaḥ sarvabhavagatyupapa........ niḥśritaṃ śīlam / sarvasattveṣvapratihata kṣāntiḥ
body.translated_text: KP.24 Not speaking falsehood; addressing [others] with a smiling face first; not [...] burdens that have not been undertaken [...]; great compassion that does not weary of all beings; indefatigable mind; insatiable pursuit of the true <s>Dharma</s> [...]; [attention to] the meaning of what has been heard; seeing faults in one's own stumbles; not angrily accusing others of their stumbles; cultivating <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) in all forms of deportment; generosity without expectation of ripening; moral conduct that is free from [attachment to] all states of existence and destinies of rebirth [...]; patience that is unobstructed toward all beings;

body.text:
KP.25 sarvakuśalamūlasamādānanāya vīryaṃ / ārūpya........ parikarṣitaṃ dhyānām /
upāyasaṅgṛhītā prajñā / catuḥsaṅgrahavastusamprayuktā upāya / śīlavaddūḥśī ............ yatayā maitratā / satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇaṃ / satkṛtyāraṇyavāsaḥ sarvalokavicitrikeṣvanabhiratiḥ...... dṛṣṭivigataṃ / hīnayānaspṛhaṇatā / mahāyāne cānuśaṃsasandarśitayā / pāpamitravivarjanat........... kalyāṇamitrasevanatā / catubrahmavihāraniṣpādanatā / pañcābhijñavikrīḍanatā / jñānapratisaraṇatā / pratipattivipratipattisthitānā sattvānām anutsargaḥ ekāñcavacanatā / satyagurukatā / ..................... kuśalamūlasamudānatayā atṛptatā / bodhicittapūrvaṅgamatā
body.translated_text: KP.25 Vigor for the gathering of all wholesome roots; <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) cultivated through [...] the formless [absorptions]; <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) embraced by skillful means; skillful means conjoined with the four <s>saṅgrahavastus</s> (means of gathering [disciples]); <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) equally toward the virtuous and the immoral [...]; respectful hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>; respectful dwelling in the forest; non-delight in all worldly diversions; [...] free from views; not craving the lesser vehicle (<s>hīnayāna</s>); and demonstrating the benefits of the great vehicle (<s>mahāyāna</s>); avoiding bad friends [...]; resorting to good friends; accomplishing the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes); sporting in the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges); relying on knowledge; not abandoning beings established in right practice and wrong practice; speaking consistently; regarding truth with reverence; [...] insatiable gathering of wholesome roots; and making <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) the foremost [priority].

body.text: KP.26 ebhiḥ kāśyapa dvāstriṃśadbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityucyate // tatredamucyate / //
body.translated_text: KP.26 Endowed with these thirty-two qualities, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> is called a <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being). Herein it is said: //

body.text:
sarveṣu satveṣu hitaṃ sukham ca adhyāśayenāpyadhimucyamānāḥ
sarvajñajñānottaraṇāya kiṃ nu arghāmi nārghāmyahaṃ jñānamānā /
akutsan. yānadhimānatāyā dṛḍhāśayākṛtrimaprematāyāḥ
sattveṣu cātyantasumitratāyā yāvanna nirvāṇaparāyaṇatvaṃ 2
mitre amitre samacittatāyā smitomukhatvam anṛtā ca vāṇī /
upātabhāre.............. dāryaṇatvaṃ karuṇāparicchinna tatheva sattve 3
body.translated_text: Aspiring with sincere intention to the benefit and happiness of all beings, [thinking] 'Am I worthy or am I not worthy of attaining the supreme omniscient knowledge?' — free from contempt, from pride regarding the vehicle, of firm intention, of genuine love, of supreme friendship toward beings, and not inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 2. Equanimity of mind toward friend and foe, a smiling countenance, and truthful speech; bearing the burden [...] compassion undiminished, likewise toward beings. 3

body.text:
KP.27 saddharmaparyeṣṭiya nāsti khedaḥ
śruteṣvatṛpte skhalitetmadoṣ........
........ raśca ruṣṭena na codanīyaḥ
īryāpathe cittasukarmatāyā 4
tyāgo vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇaṃ ca
ana............ taṃ śīladbhavaṃ gatīṣu
sattveṣu kṣānti pratighātavarjitā
samudānanāyā kuśalasya vīrya 5
ārūpyadhā........ vakṛṣṭaṃ ca dhyānaṃ
upāyato saṅgṛhītā ca prajñāḥ
catuḥsaṅgraheḥ saṅgrahītopāyo
duḥśīlaśīle dvayā.......... ca maitryā 6
satkṛtya dharmaśravaṇaṃ ca kāle satkṛtya vāso ca araṇyaśānte /
lokeṣu citreṣu ratirna kāryam hīneṣu yāneṣu ratirna kāryam 7
udārayāneṣu spṛhā janeyā pāpāṇi mitrāṇi vivarjayeyā /

children.text: kalyāṇamitrāṇi sadā ca seveś catvāra brahāśca vihāra bhāvayet / 8
children.translated_text: Good friends should always be resorted to; and the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) should be cultivated. 8

body.translated_text: KP.27 There is no weariness in the pursuit of the true <s>Dharma</s>; insatiable regarding what has been heard; when one stumbles, [acknowledging] one's own fault [...]; even when angered, one should not be harsh; skillfulness of mind in one's conduct. 4. Generosity without expectation of the ripening [of merit]; and [...] moral conduct born in [all] states of existence; patience toward beings, free from hostility; vigor in the joyful accumulation of wholesome [qualities]. 5. Meditation withdrawn from the formless realm [...] and refined; and wisdom gathered through skillful means; the means of gathering [beings] through the four means of attraction (<s>catuhsaṅgraha</s>); and loving-kindness toward both the immoral and the virtuous equally. 6. Respectful hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> at the proper time; respectful dwelling in the peace of the forest; no delight should be taken in the varied [pleasures of] the world; no delight should be taken in the lesser vehicles. 7. Aspiration for the great vehicle should be generated; evil friends should be abandoned.

body.text:
KP.28 krīḍetābhījñehi ca pañcabhiḥ sadā jñānānusāri ca bhāaveta........
na utsṛjeyā pratipattiyuktā na ca dvitīyāpi kadācid anyāḥ 9
ekāntavādī ca bhaveta nityaṃ satye ca segaurava nitya bhoti /

children.text: bhāveti dharmāṃśca jinapraśastā pūrvaṅgamaṃ bodhayi śitta kṛtvā 10
children.translated_text: One should cultivate the <s>dharmas</s> praised by the <s>Jina</s>, having made the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) foremost. 10

children.text: dvāstriṃśad ete sugatena proktā dharmā niṣevyā sugatoraseti /
children.translated_text: These thirty-two [qualities] have been declared by the <s>Sugata</s> as <s>dharmas</s> to be cultivated by the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: imehi dharmehi samanvitā ye te bodhisattvā sugatena proktā 11 //
children.translated_text: Those who are endowed with these <s>dharmas</s> — they are declared <s>bodhisattvas</s> by the <s>Sugata</s>. 11 //

body.translated_text: KP.28 One should always sport with the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges); and one should develop [...] following knowledge. One should not abandon the practice joined [with wisdom]; nor should one ever [resort to] a second, other [path]. 9. One should always be a teacher of the definitive meaning; and one should always be respectful toward truth.

body.text: KP.29 upamopanyāsanirdeśāste kāśyapa nirdekṣyāmi / yairupamopanyāsanirdeśebhiḥ bodhisattvo mahāsattvaguṇān vijñāpay..... tad yathā kāśyapa iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī sarvasattvopajīvyā nirvikārā niṣpratikārā / evam eva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisatvo yāvadbodhimaṇḍaniṣadanātāvat sarvasattvopajīvyo nirvikāro niṣpratikāro bhavati / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.29 I shall teach you, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the instruction through the presentation of similes, by which similes the qualities of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> are made known. Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this great earth is the sustenance of all beings, without distortion and without resentment — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> from the first generation of the mind [of awakening] until sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>) is the sustenance of all beings, without distortion and without resentment. Herein it is said: //

children.text: pṛthivī yathā sarvajānopajīvyā pratikāra nākāṅkṣati nirvikārā /
children.translated_text: Just as the earth is the sustenance of all people, without resentment, without distortion,

children.text: citte tathādye sthitā bodhisattvo yāvanna buddho bhavitā jinottama /
children.translated_text: so the <s>bodhisattva</s>, established in that first [awakening-]mind, until he becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, the supreme conqueror,

children.text: anuttarā sarvajanopajīvyo pratikāra nākāṅkṣati nirvikāro /
children.translated_text: unsurpassed, the sustenance of all people, not expecting reward, without distortion,

children.text: putre ca śatruṃ hi ca tulyamāna so paryeṣate nitya varāgrabodhim 2 //
children.translated_text: regarding son and enemy alike — he always seeks the supreme, foremost awakening. 2 //

body.text: KP.30 tadyathā kāśyapa abdhātu sarvatṛṇagulmoṣadhivanaspatayo rohāpayati / evam eva kāśyapa āśayaśuddho bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvāni maitratayā spharitvā viharan sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaśukladharmān virohayati / tatredamucyate
body.translated_text: KP.30 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the water element causes all grasses, shrubs, herbs, and trees to grow — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention, dwelling having pervaded all beings with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), causes all wholesome qualities (<s>śukladharma</s>) of all beings to grow. Herein it is said:

body.text:
yathāpi ābdhātu tṛṇagulmamauṣadhī vanaspatīn auṣadhidhānyajātam /
evameva śuddhāśayabodhisattvo maitryāya sattvān spharate anantāt
spharitva dharmān vividhā krameṇa

children.text: śuklehi dharmehi vivardhamānaḥ
children.translated_text: increasing in wholesome qualities,

children.text: a................ rva prāpnoti jināna bodhiṃ
children.translated_text: [...] attaining the awakening of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: nihatya mārāṃ sabalāṃ sasainyam 2 //
children.translated_text: having vanquished <s>Māra</s> together with his forces and army. 2 //

body.translated_text: Just as the water element [causes] grasses, shrubs, herbs, trees, and all kinds of medicinal grains to grow — even so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention pervades beings with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) boundlessly; having pervaded them, [he causes] various <s>dharmas</s> to [grow] in succession,

body.text: KP.31 tadyathā kāśyapa tejodhātuḥ sarvasasyāni paripā X yati / evameva kāśyapa bodhisattvasya prajñā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaśukladharmān paripācayati / tatredamucyate 3 //
body.translated_text: KP.31 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fire element ripens all crops — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s> ripens all wholesome qualities of all beings. Herein it is said: 3 //

children.text: yathāpi teja paripācayanti sasyāṇi sarvāṇi tṛṇauṣadhīṃśca /
children.translated_text: Just as fire ripens all crops, grasses, and herbs,

children.text: emeva prajñā sugatātmajānān dharmān śubhā vardhayate janasya 1 //
children.translated_text: even so, the wisdom of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> causes the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> to increase among people. 1 //

body.text: KP.32 tadyathā kāśyapa vāyudhātuḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrāni viṭhapayati evameva kāśyapa bodhisattvasyopāyakauśalyaṃ sarvabuddhadharmān viṭhapayati / tatredamucyate /
body.translated_text: KP.32 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the wind element pervades all <s>Buddha</s>-fields — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s> pervades all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. Herein it is said:

body.text:
// vāyuryatheva viṭhapeti kṣetrād buddhāna nānāvidha āśayato /
upāya evaṃ hi jinorasānān viṭhapanti dharmān sugatoktam agrān //
body.translated_text: // Just as the wind pervades the fields of the <s>Buddhas</s> in various ways according to their dispositions, even so the skillful means of the sons of the <s>Jina</s> pervades the supreme <s>dharmas</s> taught by the <s>Sugata</s>. //

body.text: KP.33 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa mārasya pāpīmataścaturaṅgaṃ balasainya sarvadevairna śakyam abhibhavituṃ paryādatuṃ vā / evameva kāśyapa śuddhāśayo bodhisattva sarvamārairna śakyam abhibhavitu paryādattuṃ vā /
body.translated_text: KP.33 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the four-division army of <s>Māra</s> the Evil One cannot be overcome or destroyed by all the gods — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention cannot be overcome or destroyed by all the <s>Māras</s>.

body.text: KP.34 // tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa śuklapakṣe candramaṇḍalaṃ paripūryate vardhate ca / evameva kāśyapa āśayaśuddho bodhisattvaḥ sarvaśukladharmairvardhate / tatredamucyate 4
body.translated_text: KP.34 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the disc of the moon is filled and increases during the bright fortnight (<s>śuklapakṣa</s>) — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention increases in all wholesome qualities. Herein it is said: 4

body.text:
// śuklapakṣe yathā candramaṇḍalaṃ............
pūryate vardhati no ca hīyate /
evameva śuddhāśayabodhisattvoḥ sic
śuddhehi dharmehi sadā vivardhate / //
body.translated_text: // Just as the disc of the moon in the bright fortnight [...] is filled and increases and does not wane — even so, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention always increases in pure <s>dharmas</s>. //

body.text: KP.35 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa sūryamaṇḍalam ekapramuktābhi sūryaraśmibhiḥ sattvānām avabhāsaṃ karoti / evameva kāśyapa bodhisattvam ekapramuktābhiḥ prajñāraśmibhiḥ sattvānām jñānāvabhāsaṃ karoti / tatredamucyate 7
body.translated_text: KP.35 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the disc of the sun, with rays emitted all at once, illuminates beings — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, with rays of wisdom emitted all at once, creates the illumination of knowledge for beings. Herein it is said: 7

body.text: // mekapramuktābhi yatheva sūryo

children.text: raśmībhi sattvānna sic karoti bhāsam
children.translated_text: illuminates beings with its rays,

children.text: evaṃ jinānāṃ suta jñānaraśmibhi
children.translated_text: even so the son of the <s>Jinas</s>, with rays of knowledge,

children.text: prajñāya sattvānavabhāsa kurvati //
children.translated_text: through wisdom, illuminates beings. //

body.translated_text: // Just as the sun, with rays emitted all at once,

body.text: KP.36 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa siṅho mṛgarājā yato yata / eva prakramate sarvatrābhito nutrasta evaṃ prakramati / evameva kāśyapa śīlaśrutaguṇadharmapratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo yato yata eva prakramate sarvatrābhīto nutrasta eva prakramate / tatredamucyate 8
body.translated_text: KP.36 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the lion, the king of beasts, wherever he goes, he goes everywhere fearless and undaunted — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the qualities of moral conduct, learning, and knowledge, wherever he goes, he goes everywhere fearless and undaunted. Herein it is said: 8

body.text:
// yathā hi siṅho mṛgarāja kesarī yenecchakaṃ yāti asantrasanto /
evameva śīlaṃśrutajñānasusthito sic yenecchakaṃ gacchati bodhisattvo //
body.translated_text: // Just as the lion, the king of beasts, the maned one, goes wherever he wishes, undaunted — even so the <s>bodhisattva</s>, firmly established in moral conduct, learning, and knowledge, goes wherever he wishes. //

body.text: KP.37 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa sudāntaḥ kuñjaro nāgassarvabhāravahanatayā na parikhidyate / evameva kāśyapa sudāntacitto bodhisattva sarvasattvānāṃ sarvabhāravahanatā na parikhidyate / tatredamucyate
body.translated_text: KP.37 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a well-tamed bull elephant is not wearied by carrying all burdens — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose mind is well-tamed is not wearied by carrying all the burdens of all beings. Herein it is said:

children.text: yathāpi nāmago sic balavān sudānto bhāraṃ vahanto na dupeti khedaṃ /
children.translated_text: Just as a strong, well-tamed elephant, while carrying a burden, does not incur weariness,

children.text: sudāntacitto tathā bodhisattvo sattvāna bhāreṇa na khedamaiti //
children.translated_text: so too a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose mind is well-tamed does not reach weariness from the burden of beings. //

body.text: KP.38 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa padmamudake jātamudakena na lipyate / evameva kāśyapa bodhisattvo loke jāto lokadharme na lipyate / tatredamucyate 10
body.translated_text: KP.38 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a lotus born in water is not defiled by water — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> born in the world is not defiled by worldly conditions. Herein it is said: 10

body.text:
// padmaṃ yathā kokanadaṃ jaleruhaṃ jalena no lipyati kardamena vā /
loke smi jāto tathā bodhisattvo na lokadharmehi kadāci lipyate //
body.translated_text: // Just as the lotus, the water-lily, born in water, is not defiled by water or by mud — so too a <s>bodhisattva</s> born in this world is never defiled by worldly conditions. //

body.text: KP.39 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa viṭapacchinno vṛkṣo mūle nupahate punareva virohati / evameva kāśyapa upāyakauśalyakleśacchinno bodhisattvaḥ sarvakuśalamūlasaṃyojane nupahate punareva traidhātuke virohati / tatredamucyate 11
body.translated_text: KP.39 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a tree whose branches have been cut, when its root is unharmed, grows again — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> whose afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) have been cut by skillful means, when the connection to all roots of merit is unharmed, grows again in the three realms. Herein it is said: 11

body.text:
// yathāpi vṛkṣo viṭapasmi cchinno virohate mūla dṛḍhe nupadrute /
evam upāyopahato virohate mūlasmi saṃyojana suprahīṇe //
body.translated_text: // Just as a tree cut at the branches grows again when its root is firm and unharmed — even so one whose [afflictions are] destroyed by skillful means grows again when the root, the connection [to merit], is well-abandoned. //

body.text: KP.40 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa nānādigvidikṣu mahānadīṣvāpskandho mahāsamudre praviṣṭaḥ sarvam ekaraso bhavati yaduta lavaṇarasaḥ evameva kāśyapa nānāmukhopacitaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ bodhisattvasya bodhāya pariṇāmitaṃ sarvam ekarasaṃ yadida vimuktirasaṃ / tatredamucyate 12
body.translated_text: KP.40 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the mass of water of the great rivers from various directions, having entered the great ocean, all becomes of one taste — namely, the taste of salt — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, roots of merit accumulated through various means by a <s>bodhisattva</s>, when dedicated to awakening, all become of one taste — namely, the taste of liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). Herein it is said: 12

body.text:
// nānānadīnām udakaṃ praviṣṭaṃ mahāsamudrekarasaṃ yathā syāt
kuśalāni nānāmukhasañcitāni parināmitānyekarasāni bodhye //
body.translated_text: // Just as the waters of various rivers, having entered the great ocean, become of one taste — so too wholesome [roots] accumulated through various means, when dedicated to awakening, become of one taste. //

body.text: KP.41 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa sumerupratiṣṭhitā caturmahārājakāyikāstrayastriṃśāśca devāḥ evameva kāśyapa bodhicittākuśalamūlapratiṣṭhitā bodhisattvasya sarvajñatā tatredamucyate 13
body.translated_text: KP.41 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heavens are established on <s>Sumeru</s> — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s> is established on the roots of merit [arising from] the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). Herein it is said: 13

body.text:
// caturmahārājikas sic trāyastriñcā yath. sumerusthita devasaṅghā /
tatha bodhisattvā kuśale pratiṣṭhāḥ sarvajñatā prāpya vadanti dharmān //
body.translated_text:
Just as the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> and <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods dwell upon <s>Sumeru</s>,
so too <s>bodhisattvas</s> established in virtue, having attained omniscience, teach the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: KP.42 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa āmātyasaṅgṛhītā rājānaḥ sarvarājakāryāṇi kurvanti / evameva kāśyapa upāyasaṅgṛhītā bodhisattvasya prajñā sarvabuddhakāryāṇi karoti / tatredamucyate 14
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, kings supported by ministers carry out all royal duties, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the wisdom of a <s>bodhisattva</s> supported by skillful means carries out all the work of a <s>Buddha</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// yathā hi rājāna āmātyasaṅgrahā sarvāṇi kāryāṇi karoti nityaṃ /
tatha sic bodhisattvasya upāyasaṅgraho buddhārtha prajñāya karonti nitya //
body.translated_text:
Just as a king, supported by ministers, always carries out all duties,
so too the wisdom of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, supported by skillful means, always accomplishes the purpose of a <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: KP.43 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa vyabhre deve vigatavalāhake nāsti varṣasyāyadvāram evameva kāśyapa alpaśrutasya bodhisattvasyāntikānāsti saddharmavṛṣṭerāryadvaraṃ / tatredamucyate 15
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, when the sky is clear and free of clouds, there is no occasion for rain, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in the presence of a <s>bodhisattva</s> of little learning, there is no noble occasion for the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// vyabhre yathā vigatavalāhake nabhe varṣasya ā............ na kadāci vidyate /
alpaśrutasyāntikad sic dharmadeśanā na bodhisattvasya kadāci labhyate //
body.translated_text:
Just as when the sky is clear and free of clouds, rain [...] is never found,
so too the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> is never obtained in the presence of a <s>bodhisattva</s> of little learning.

body.text: KP.44 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa.......... bhraghanameghasamutthitā varṣadhārā sasyānyabhivarṣati / evameva kāśyapa mahākaruṇādharmameghasamutth......... bodhisattvasya saddharmavṛṣṭissattvānām abhivarṣati / tatredamucyate 16
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, [...] a stream of rain arisen from dense thick clouds showers upon the crops, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, arisen from the cloud of great compassion and <s>Dharma</s> [...], showers upon beings. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: yathāpi megho vipulo savidyuto ...........
children.translated_text: Just as a vast cloud with lightning [...]

children.text: syānuvarṣeṇa karoti tṛptim /
children.translated_text: satisfies with its continuous rain,

children.text: saddharmameghotthitavarṣadhārā
children.translated_text: the stream of rain arisen from the cloud of the true <s>Dharma</s>

children.text: tarpeti satvāstatha bodhisatvaḥ //
children.translated_text: satisfies beings, so does the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: KP.45 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa yatra rājā cakravarti utpadyate tatra saptaratnānyutpadyante evam eva kāśyapa yatra bodhisattva utpadyate tatra saptātriñcad bodhapakṣyā dharmā utpadyante / tatredamucyate 17
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, wherever a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch) arises, there the seven treasures arise, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, wherever a <s>bodhisattva</s> arises, there the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening arise. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// utpadyate yatra hi cakravarti tatrāsya ratnāni bhavanti sapta
utpadyate yatra ca bodhisattvas tatrāsya bodhyaṅga bhavanti sapta //
body.translated_text:
Wherever a <s>cakravartin</s> arises, there his seven treasures come to be;
wherever a <s>bodhisattva</s> arises, there his seven factors of awakening come to be.

body.text: KP.46 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa yatra maṇiratnāyadvāraṃ bhavati bahūnāṃ tatra kārṣāpaṇaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhavati / evameva kāśyapa yatra bodhisattvasyāyadvāraṃ bhavati / bahūnām tatra śrāvakapratyekabuddhahaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhavati / tatredamucyate 18
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, wherever there is an occasion for a jewel-gem, there is an occasion for many hundreds of thousands of <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins), even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, wherever there is an occasion for a <s>bodhisattva</s>, there is an occasion for many hundreds of thousands of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // yathāpi yasmiṃ maṇiratna bhoti /

children.text: karṣāpaṇāyo bahu............ tra bhoti
children.translated_text: many <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> [...] exist there,

children.text: sambodhicittasya ca yatra āyo
children.translated_text: and where there is income from the thought of perfect awakening,

children.text: āyo bahū tatra ca śrāvakānām //
children.translated_text: there is abundant income for <s>śrāvakas</s> as well.

body.translated_text: Just as where a jewel-gem exists,

body.text: KP.47 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa miśrakāvanapratiṣṭhitānā trāyastriṃśānāṃ devānām upabhogaparibhogāḥ samāḥ santiṣṭhante / evameva kāśyapa āśayaśuddhasya bodhisattvasya sarvasattvānām antike samyakprayogo bhavati / tatredamucyate 19
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, for the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods dwelling in the <s>Miśrakāvana</s> (Mixed Grove), enjoyments and possessions remain equal, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention engages in right practice toward all beings equally. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// yathāpi devāna samā prayogā miśrāvane saṃsthihate sthitānā
evameva śuddhāsaya bodhisattvo satveṣu samyakkurute prayogam //
body.translated_text:
Just as the practice of the gods dwelling in <s>Miśrakāvana</s> is equal,
even so a <s>bodhisattva</s> of pure intention engages in right practice toward beings.

body.text: KP.48 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa mantrauṣadhaparigṛhītaṃ viṣaṃ na vinipātayati / evameva kāśyapa jñānopāyakauśalyaparigṛhīto bodhisattvasya kleśaviṣaṃ na śaknoti vinipātayitum / tatredamucyate 20
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, poison that is counteracted by mantras and herbs does not cause destruction, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the poison of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) counteracted by the skill in means of knowledge is unable to destroy a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// yathā viṣam mantraparigraheṇa janasya doṣaṃ kriyayāsamarthaṃ
evaṃ hi jñānī iha bodhisattvo kleśairna śakyaṃ vinipātanāya / //
body.translated_text:
Just as poison, through the power of mantras, is unable to cause harm to a person,
even so a <s>bodhisattva</s> who possesses knowledge cannot be destroyed by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).

body.text: KP.49 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa yaṃ mahānagareṣu saṅkarakūtaṃ bhavati sa ikṣukṣetreṣu śālikṣetreṣu mṛdvīkākṣetreṣu copakārībhūte bhavati / evameva kāśyapa yo bodhisattvasya kleśaḥ sa sarvajñatāyām upakārībhuto bhavati / tatredamucyate // 21
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the refuse heap that exists in great cities becomes beneficial for sugarcane fields, rice fields, and grape fields, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of a <s>bodhisattva</s> become beneficial for omniscience. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// nagareṣu saṅkāruryathā sucokṣo so ikṣukṣetreṣupakāra kurvati /
evameva kleśo upakārā kurvati yo bodhisattvasya jināna dharme //
body.translated_text:
Just as refuse in cities, when well-purified, serves as benefit for sugarcane fields,
even so the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) serve as benefit for a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones).

body.text: KP.50 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa iṣvastre aśikṣitasya śastragrahaṇam evameva kāśyapa alpaśrutasya bodhisattvasya dharmapravicayakauśalyamīmāsadarthagrahaṇajñānaṃ draṣṭavyaḥ 22 //
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, for one untrained in archery, grasping a weapon is dangerous, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, for a <s>bodhisattva</s> of little learning, the knowledge of grasping the meaning through investigation and examination of the <s>Dharma</s> should be regarded in the same way.

body.text: KP.51 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa kumbhakārasya bālabhājaneṣūdārāgnidānām evameva kāśyapa bālaprajñeṣu bodhisattvasyodāradharmadeśanā sic veditavyaḥ 22 //
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, for a potter placing unfired vessels in a great fire, even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, one should understand the teaching of profound <s>Dharma</s> to <s>bodhisattvas</s> of immature wisdom in the same way.

body.text: KP.52 tasmin tarhi kāśyapa iha mahāratnakūṭe dharmaparyāye śikṣitukāmena bodhisattvena yoniśo dharmaprayuktena bhavitavyaṃ / tatra kāśyapa katamo yoniśadharmaprayogaḥ yaduta sarvadharmāṇāṃ bhutapratyavekṣā / katamā ca kāśyapa sarvadharmāṇāṃ bhutapratyavekṣā / yatra kāśyapa nātmapratyave kṣānasattvanajīvanapoṣanapudgalanamanujanamānavāpratyavekṣā / iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā /
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to train in this <s>Mahāratnakūṭa</s> (Great Heap of Jewels) <s>Dharma</s> discourse must engage properly with the <s>Dharma</s>. And what, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is proper engagement with the <s>Dharma</s>? It is the true examination of all <s>dharmas</s>. And what, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the true examination of all <s>dharmas</s>? That which, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is neither the examination of self, nor of a being, nor of a living soul, nor of a nourisher, nor of a person, nor of a human, nor of a man -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.53 punaraparaṃ kāśyapa maddhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā yā rūpasya na nityam iti pratyavekṣā nānityānīti pratyavekṣā / yā vedanāyāḥ sañjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vijñānasya na nityam iti pratyavekṣā / nānityam iti pratyavekṣā iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>, is the examination of <s>rūpa</s> (form) as neither permanent nor impermanent. That which is the examination of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as neither permanent nor impermanent -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.54 yā pṛthivīdhātorna nityam iti pratyavekṣā nānityam iti pratyavekṣā yābdhātostejodhātorvāyudhāto na nityam iti pratyavekṣā nānityam iti pratyavekṣā / yā ākāśadhātorvijñānadhāto na nityam iti pratyavekṣā nānityam iti pratyavekṣā iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā /
body.translated_text: That which is the examination of the earth element as neither permanent nor impermanent, that which is the examination of the water element, fire element, and wind element as neither permanent nor impermanent, that which is the examination of the space element and consciousness element as neither permanent nor impermanent -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.55 punaraparaṃ kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā / yā cakṣurāyatanasya na nityam iti pratyavekṣā nānityam iti pratyavekṣā iyam ucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā / evaṃ yāvacchrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanāyatanasya na nityam ityam iti / pratyavekṣā iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>: that which is the examination of the eye sense-base as neither permanent nor impermanent -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise, up to the examination of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind sense-bases as neither permanent nor impermanent -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.56 nityam iti kāśyapa ayam eko 'ntaḥ anityam iti kāśyapa ayaṃ dvitīyo 'ntaḥ yadetayordvayo nityānityayormadhyaṃ tadarūpyanidarśanam anābhāsam avijñāptikam apratiṣṭham aniketam iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā /
body.translated_text: 'Permanent' -- <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is one extreme. 'Impermanent' -- <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is the second extreme. That which is the middle between these two, permanence and impermanence, is formless, without indication, without appearance, without cognizance, without foundation, without abode -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.57 ātmeti kāśyapa ayam eko 'ntaḥ nairātmyam ityayaṃ dvitīyo 'ntaḥ yadātmanairātmyayormadhyaṃ tadarūpyanidarśanam anābhāsam avijñaptikam apratiṣṭham aniketam iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā /
body.translated_text: 'Self' -- <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is one extreme. 'Non-self' -- this is the second extreme. That which is the middle between self and non-self is formless, without indication, without appearance, without cognizance, without foundation, without abode -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.58 bhūtacittam iti kāśyapa ayam eko 'ntaḥ abhūtacittam iti kāśyapa ayaṃ dvitīyo 'ntaḥ yatra kāśyapa na cetanā na mano na vijñānam iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhutapratyavekṣā
body.translated_text: 'The mind is real' -- <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is one extreme. 'The mind is unreal' -- <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is the second extreme. Where, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, there is neither volition, nor mind, nor consciousness -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.59 evaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ kuśalākuśalānāṃ lokikalokottarāṇāṃ sāvadyānavadyānāṃ sāsravānāsravānāṃ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtānāṃ saṅkleśa iti kāśyapa ayam eko 'ntaḥ vyavadānam ityayam kāśyapa dvitīyo 'ntaḥ yo syāntadvayasyānugamo nudāhāro pravyāhāra iyamucyate / kāśyapa madhyāmā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā /
body.translated_text: Thus, of all <s>dharmas</s> -- wholesome and unwholesome, mundane and supramundane, blameworthy and blameless, with outflows and without outflows, conditioned and unconditioned -- 'defilement,' <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is one extreme; 'purification,' <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is the second extreme. That which is neither following after nor articulating nor uttering these two extremes -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.60 astīti kāśyapa ayam eko 'ntaḥ nāstityayaṃ dvitīyo 'ntaḥ yadetayordvayorantayormadhyam iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣat
body.translated_text: 'It exists' -- <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this is one extreme. 'It does not exist' -- this is the second extreme. That which is the middle between these two extremes -- this is called, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>madhyamā pratipad</s> (middle way), the true examination of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.61 yadapi kāśyapa yuṣmākaṃ mayākhyāta / yaduta avidyāpratyayā saṃskārāḥ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ vijñānapratyayan nāmārūpannāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ ṣaḍāyatanapratyaya sparśaḥ saparśaprapratyayā vedanā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānam upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ bhavapratyayā jātiḥ jātipratyayā jarāmaroṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ sambhavantyevam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati /
body.translated_text: KP.61 Moreover, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, what I have taught to you — namely, that from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as condition arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); from <s>saṃskāras</s> as condition arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); from <s>vijñāna</s> as condition arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); from <s>nāmarūpa</s> as condition arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases); from the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> as condition arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); from <s>sparśa</s> as condition arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); from <s>vedanā</s> as condition arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); from <s>tṛṣṇā</s> as condition arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); from <s>upādāna</s> as condition arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); from <s>bhava</s> as condition arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); from <s>jāti</s> as condition arise <s>jarā</s> (aging), <s>maraṇa</s> (death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and distress — thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering.

body.text:
KP.62 avidyānirodhā saṃskāranirodhaḥ saṃskāranirodhādvijñānanirodhaḥ vijñānanirodhānnāmarūpanirodhaḥ nāmarūpanirodhātṣaḍāyatanani ........................... .........................................
cyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipaddharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣā //
body.translated_text: KP.62 From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); from the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> comes the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); from the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> comes the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); from the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s> comes the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases) [...] This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>), the true investigation of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.63 punaraparaṃ kāśyapa dharmāṇāṃ bhutapratyavekṣā yanna śunyatāyā dharmā śūnyā karoti dharmā eva śūnyā / yannānimittena dharmān animittān karoti dharmā caivānimittāḥ yannāpraṇihitena dharmā / praṇihitān karoti dharmā evāpraṇihitāḥ yannānabhisaṃskāreṇa dharmān abhisaṃskaroti dharmā cavānabhisaṃskṛtāḥ evaṃ nānutpadena dharmānnānutpādā karoti dharmā caivānutpannāḥ evaṃ najātā dharmān ajātīkaroti dharmā caivājātaḥ eva yanna agrāhyā dharmānnagrāhyā karoti dharmā caivāgrāhyā / evam anāsravā dharmān anāsravā karoti dharmā caivānāsravā / evaṃ yo nasvabhāvena dharmān asvabhāvikaroti dharmā caivāsvabhāvā / evaṃ yanna svabhāvena dharmāsvabhāvatā dharmāṇāṃ yatsvabhāvaṃ nopalabhate yā evaṃ pratyavekṣā iyamucyate kāśyapa madhyamā pratipad dharmāṇāṃ bhūtapratyavekṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: KP.63 Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the true investigation of <s>dharmas</s> is this: it is not that <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) makes <s>dharmas</s> empty — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are empty. It is not that signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>) makes <s>dharmas</s> signless — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are signless. It is not that wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>) makes <s>dharmas</s> wishless — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are wishless. It is not that non-fabrication (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>) fabricates <s>dharmas</s> — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are unfabricated. Likewise, it is not that non-arising makes <s>dharmas</s> non-arising — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are unarisen. Likewise, it is not that the unborn makes <s>dharmas</s> unborn — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are unborn. Likewise, it is not that the ungraspable makes <s>dharmas</s> ungraspable — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are ungraspable. Likewise, it is not that the undefiled makes <s>dharmas</s> undefiled — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are undefiled. Likewise, it is not that own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) makes <s>dharmas</s> without own-nature — <s>dharmas</s> themselves are without own-nature. Likewise, it is the very <s>svabhāvatā</s> (own-nature-ness) of <s>dharmas</s> that is not found as own-nature through own-nature. Such investigation — this, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the middle path, the true investigation of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.64 na khalu punaḥ kāśyapa pudgalabhāvavināśāya śūnyatā pudgalaścaiva śūnyatā śūnyatā caiva śūnyatā / atyantaśūnyatā / purvāntaśūnyatā / aparāntaśūnyatā pratyutpannaśūnyatā / śūnyatā kāśyapa pratisaratha mā pudgalam / ye khalu puna kāśyapaḥ śūnyatopalambhena śūnyatā pratisaranti / tān ahaṃ kāśyapa naṣṭapranaṣṭān iti vadāmi ito pravacanāt / varaṃ khalu puna kāśyapa sumerumātrā pudgaladṛṣṭirāśritā na tyevādhimānikasya śūnyatādṛṣṭimālinā / tatkasmāddheto pudgaladṛṣṭigatānām kāśyapa śūnyatā niḥsaraṇaṃ śunyatādṛṣṭi puna kāśyapa kena niḥsariṣyantiḥ //
body.translated_text: KP.64 Indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is not for the destruction of the being of a person — the person itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is emptiness. It is absolute emptiness, emptiness of the past, emptiness of the future, emptiness of the present. <s>Kāśyapa</s>, take refuge in <s>śūnyatā</s>, not in [the notion of] a person. But those, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who take refuge in <s>śūnyatā</s> with the apprehension of emptiness — those I call, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, lost and utterly lost from this teaching. Indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, it is better to have a view of the person as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> than to have the view of emptiness held by one who is conceited. Why? Because for those who have fallen into the view of a person, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> is the way out. But those who hold the view of emptiness, <s>Kāśyapa</s> — by what will they escape?

body.text: KP.65 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa kaścid eva puruṣo glāno bhavet / tasmai vaidyo bhaiṣajyaṃ dadyāt tasya tad bhaiṣajyaṃ sarvadoṣā ucālya koṣṭhagata na nirgacchet tatkiṃ manyase kāśyapa api nu sa glānapuruṣastasmād glānyā parimukto bhavet / yasya tad bhaiṣajyaṃ sarvakoṣṭhagatā doṣān uccālya koṣṭhagato na niḥsaret / āha no bhagavān / gāḍhataraśca tasya puruṣasya tadgelānyaṃ bhavet / yasya tad bhaiṣajyaṃ sarvadoṣān ucālya sakoṣṭhagataṃ na niḥsaret / bhagavān āha / evameva kāśyapa sarvadṛṣṭigatānāṃ śūnyatā niḥsaraṇaṃ yasya khalu punaḥ kāśyapa śūnyatādṛṣṭistam aham acikitsyam iti vadāmi / tatredamucyate / //
body.translated_text: KP.65 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain man were ill. A physician would give him medicine. That medicine would stir up all the morbid humors in his body but would not pass out. What do you think, <s>Kāśyapa</s> — would that sick man be freed from his illness, if that medicine, having stirred up all the morbid humors in his body, did not pass out? He replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One). That man's illness would become even more severe, if that medicine, having stirred up all the morbid humors, remained within the body and did not pass out. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> is the way out from all views. But one who holds emptiness as a view — that one I call incurable. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
yathā hi vaidyo puruṣasya dadyādd virecanaṃ rogavinigrahāya
uccālya doṣāśca na niḥsareta tato nidānaṃ ca na copaśānti /
// imeva dṛṣṭigahanāśṛteṣu yā śunyatā niḥsaraṇaṃ paraṃ hi /
sāśu ................................

Just as a physician might give a man a purgative to subdue illness,
and it stirs up the morbid humors but does not pass out — then the cause [of illness] is not pacified.
Likewise, for those entangled in the thicket of views, <s>śūnyatā</s> is indeed the supreme escape,
but that very [emptiness], if [...] [text incomplete]

body.text: KP.70 ...................................................................................... ye pi śūnyaṃ / // tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa tailapradīpasyaivaṃ bhavatyaham andhakāraṃ vidhamāmīti / athā ca punastailapradyote kṛte ālokaṃ pratītya tamondhakāraṃ vigacchati / yaśca kāśyapa tailapradyoto yaśca tamondhakāram ubhāyam etac śūnyatā / agrāhyā śūnya niśceṣṭāḥ evameva kāśyapa yaṃ ca jñānaṃ cājñānaṃ cājñānaṃ ca ubhayam etac śūnyad agrāhyā śūnyā niśceṣṭyā 7 /
body.translated_text: KP.70 [...] which is empty. It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, an oil lamp — thus it would think: 'I dispel darkness.' But when the oil lamp is lit, it is in dependence on light that the darkness and gloom depart. <s>Kāśyapa</s>, both the oil lamp and the darkness and gloom — both these are <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness): ungraspable, empty, and without activity. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, both knowledge and ignorance — both these are empty: ungraspable, empty, and without activity.

body.text: KP.71 // tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa gṛhe vā layane vā avavarake vā varṣāsahasrasyātyayena na tat kadācit tailapradyotaḥ kṛto bhavet / atha ca tatra kaścid eva puruṣaḥ tailapradīpaṃ kuryāt / tatkiṃ manyase kāśyapa maivāṃ tasya tamondhakārasya bhūdvarṣāsahasrasañcito 'haṃ nāham ito vigamiṣyāmīti / āha no hīdaṃ bhagavan na....... tasya tamondhakārasya śaktirasti yastailapradyota kṛte na vigantum avaśyaṃ tena vigatavyaṃ bhagavān āha evameva kāśyapa kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrasañcito 'pi karmakleśa ekena yoniśomanasikāraprajñāpratyavekṣaṇena vigacchati / tailapradyota iti kāśyapa āryasyaitat prajñendriyasyādhivacanaṃ / tamondhakāra iti kāśyapatkarmakleśasyādhivacanam / tatredamucyate 8
body.translated_text: KP.71 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in a house, or a cave, or a chamber, after the passage of a thousand years, no oil lamp had ever been lit therein. Then a certain man were to light an oil lamp there. What do you think, <s>Kāśyapa</s> — would that darkness think: 'I have been accumulated over a thousand years; I shall not depart from here'? He replied: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. That darkness does not have the power [...] not to depart when the oil lamp is lit — it must necessarily depart. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, even <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions) accumulated over a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (eons) are dispelled by a single [moment of] wise attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>) and investigation by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). 'Oil lamp,' <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a designation for the <s>prajñendriya</s> (faculty of wisdom) of a noble one. 'Darkness and gloom,' <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a designation for <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśa</s>. Regarding this, it is said:
Just as a lamp in a chamber, long [in darkness], lit by some person [...] [text incomplete]
