body.text: KP.78 // tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa ghuṇṇakhāditasya sarṣapam abhyamtare ākāśadhātu evameva kāśyapa śrāvakasyābhisaṃskṛtaṃ jñānaṃ draṣṭavya / tatredamucyate 14
body.translated_text: KP.78 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, within a worm-eaten mustard seed there is the space element. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, should the conditioned knowledge of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) be understood. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// ghuṇakhāditasyaiva hi sarṣapasya ākāśam abhyantaritopariktaṃ /
abhisaṃskṛtaṃ jñāna tathā vijānatha yaṃ śrāvakasya laghukaṃ pariktaktaṃ //
body.translated_text:
Just as within a worm-eaten mustard seed, the space inside and above is [tiny],
so understand the conditioned knowledge of the <s>śrāvaka</s>, which is small and limited.

body.text: KP.79 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa daśāsu dikṣvākāśadhāturevaṃ bodhisattvasyābhisaṃskṛtaṃ jñānaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ / tatredamucyate 15
body.translated_text: KP.79 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the space element in the ten directions — just so should the conditioned knowledge of a <s>bodhisattva</s> be understood. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// yathāpi ākāśa daśadiśāsu anāvṛtaṃ tiṣṭhati sarvaloke /
abhisaṃskṛtaṃ paśyatha bodhisattve jñānaṃ tathā sarvajagatpradhāna / //
body.translated_text:
Just as space stands unobstructed in the ten directions throughout all the world,
so behold the conditioned knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva</s> — foremost in all the world.

body.text: KP.80 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasyāgramahiṣi daridrapuruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ vipratipadyeta tasya tataḥ putro jāyetaḥ tatkiṃ manyase kāśyapa api nu sa rājaputra iti vaktavyaḥ āha no hīdaṃ bhagavan bhagavān āha / evameva kāśyapa kiñcāpi mama śrāvakārdharmadhātunirjātā na ca punaste tathāgatasyābhiṣekyaputrā iti vaktavyāḥ tatradamucyate 16
body.translated_text: KP.80 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a chief queen of a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior-class) king who has received the royal consecration were to consort with a poor man, and from that union a son were born. What do you think, <s>Kāśyapa</s> — should that son be called a prince? He replied: No indeed, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, although my <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) are born from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>Dharma</s>), they are not to be called consecrated sons of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // yathāpi rājño mahiṣī manāpī daridrasattvena sahāvaseta /

children.text: tasyā sutastena ca jāyate yo 40b5 sa rājaputro na tu rājā bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: and the son born to her from him — he would be a prince, but he shall not become king.

children.text: evameva ye śrāvakā vītarāgā na te bhiṣekyā mama jātu putrāḥ
children.translated_text: Just so, those <s>śrāvakas</s> who are free from passion — they are never my consecrated sons.

children.text: tathā hi te ātmahitāya yuktā svaparobhayārthekarabuddhaputrāḥ //
children.translated_text: For they are devoted only to their own benefit; the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> are those who accomplish the welfare of both self and others.

body.translated_text: Just as a king's beloved chief queen might cohabit with a poor man,

body.text: KP.81 / tadyathāpi nāmā kāśyapa rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pratyavarayā ceṭikayā sahā pratipadyeta / tasya tata putra utpadyeta / kiñcāpi kāśyapa sa pratyavarayā ceṭikayā sāntikādutpanno tha ca puna sa rājaputra iti vaktavyaḥ evameva kāśyapa kiñcāpi prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ apratibalaḥ saṃsāre saṃsaran sattvān vinayi kāmamathā ca puna sa tathāgataputro iti vaktavyaḥ tatredamucyate 17
body.translated_text: KP.81 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s> king who has received the royal consecration were to consort with a lowly servant woman, and from that union a son were born. Although, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, he was born from a lowly servant woman, still he should be called a prince. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, although a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first aspiration to awakening (<s>prathamacittotpāda</s>) is not yet capable, while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, of taming and guiding beings — still he should be called a son of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // cetiyā sārdhaṃ yathā cakravarttī saṃvāsaṃ gatvā janayeta putraṃ /

children.text: kiñcāpi ceṭiyasakāśajāto taṃ rājaputreti vadeti loke /
children.translated_text: although born from a servant woman, the world calls him 'prince';

children.text: citte tathā prathame bodhisattvo balena hīno tribhave bhramanto /
children.translated_text: so too the <s>bodhisattva</s> at the first generation of mind, though lacking in strength, wandering in the three realms of existence,

children.text: dānena sattvāvinayann upāyair jinātmajo vuccati śuddhasattvoḥ 3 //
children.translated_text: taming beings through generosity and skillful means, is called a son of the <s>Jina</s>, a pure being.

body.translated_text: Just as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), having united with a servant woman, would beget a son —

body.text: KP.82 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa rājñā cakravartinaḥ putrasahasraṃ bhavet / na cātra kaścicakravartilakṣaṇasamanvāgato bhavet / na tatra rājñaścakravartinaḥ putrasañjñā manyeta / evameva kāśyapa kiñcāpi tathāgato koṭiśatasahasraparivāraḥ śrāvakerna cātra kaścid bodhisattvo bhavati na tatra tathāgatasya putrasañjñotpadyate / tatredamucyate 18
body.translated_text: KP.82 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a king who is a <s>cakravartin</s> might have a thousand sons, yet none of them would be endowed with the marks of a <s>cakravartin</s> — the king, the <s>cakravartin</s>, would not regard any of them with the perception of a [true] son. Even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, although the <s>Tathāgata</s> is surrounded by hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), yet none of them is a <s>bodhisattva</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not generate the perception of a son regarding them. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // yathā sahasraṃ nṛpate sutānāṃ na ceka putro 'pi salakṣaṇaḥ syāt /

children.text: na tatra sañjñā nṛvarasya teṣu voḍhū yataste na dhuraṃ samarthāḥ
children.translated_text: the lord of men would have no [filial] regard for them, since they are not able to bear the burden;

children.text: tathā hi buddho bahukoṭinirvṛtaḥ syāt teṣu kaścinna ca bodhisattvaḥ
children.translated_text: even so, the <s>Buddha</s>, though surrounded by many <s>koṭis</s>, yet among them there is no <s>bodhisattva</s> —

children.text: na putrasañjñā sugatasya teṣu na bodhisattvo 'sti yato tra kaścit 2 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sugata</s> has no perception of a son regarding them, since there is no <s>bodhisattva</s> among them.

body.translated_text: Just as a king has a thousand sons, yet not even one of them would possess the [auspicious] marks —

body.text: KP.83 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa rājñaścakravartino agramahiṣyā kukṣe saptarātropapannaḥ kumāraścakravartilakṣaṇasamanvāgataḥ tasya kukṣigatasyāparipakvendriyasya kalalamahābhūtagatasya balavantatarā tatra devatā spṛhām utpādayanti / na tveva teṣu balajavanavegasthāmaprāpteṣu kumāreṣu tatkasmāddheto sa hi cakravartivaṃśasyānupacchedāya sthāsyati / evameva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ aparipakvendriya kalalamahābhūtagata eva samānodatha ca punarbalavantatarā tatra pūrvadarśano devā spṛhām utpādayanti / na tvevāṣṭavimokṣadhyāyīṣvarhatsu / tatkasmāddhetoḥ sa hi buddhavaṃśasyānupacchedāya sthāsyati / tatredamucyate 19
body.translated_text: KP.83 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a prince conceived seven nights ago in the womb of the chief queen of a <s>cakravartin</s> king, endowed with the marks of a <s>cakravartin</s> — even while in the womb, with immature faculties, in the state of an embryonic great element — the more powerful gods generate longing toward him, but not toward those princes who have attained strength, speed, power, and might. For what reason? Because he will stand for the unbroken continuity of the <s>cakravartin</s> lineage. Even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening], even while being like an embryonic great element with immature faculties — the more powerful gods who have seen him before generate longing toward him, but not toward the <s>arhats</s> who meditate on the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations). For what reason? Because he will stand for the unbroken continuity of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // yathāgradevīya tu cakravartino kukṣisthito lakṣaṇapuṇyasattvo /

children.text: balavantaraṃ deva spṛhā karonti na sthāmaprāptāna kumārakānāṃ
children.translated_text: the more powerful gods generate longing [toward him], but not toward the princes who have attained might;

children.text: ekāgracitte sthitabodhisatve saṃsārasaṃsthe ghaṭamānabodhaye /
children.translated_text: when a <s>bodhisattva</s> is established with a one-pointed mind, dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s>, striving for awakening —

children.text: janenti tasya spṛha devanāgā na śrāvakeṣu trivimokṣadhyāyiṣu //
children.translated_text: gods and <s>nāgas</s> generate longing toward him, but not toward <s>śrāvakas</s> who meditate on the three <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations).

body.translated_text: Just as for the chief queen of a <s>cakravartin</s>, the being endowed with marks and merit, dwelling in her womb —

body.text: KP.84 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa karaviṅkapotaka āṇḍakośaprakṣipataḥ anirbhinne nayane sarvapakṣigaṇam abhibhavati / yaduta gambhīramadhuranirghoṣarutaravitet / evameva kāśyapaḥ prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvo avidyāṇḍakośaprakṣipta karmakleśatamastimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhaḥnayano 'pi sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhām abhibhavati / yaduta kuśalamūlapariṇāmanāprayoganirhārarutaravitena 20 // tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa rājñaścakravartina agramahiṣyā tatkṣaṇajātaṃ kumāraṃ sarvaśreṣṭhinaigamajānapatayaḥ koṭṭarājānaśca namasyantyevameva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ sadevako loko namaskaronti 21 //
body.translated_text: KP.84 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>karaviṅka</s> (Indian cuckoo) chick, while still enclosed in its eggshell, with eyes not yet opened, surpasses all flocks of birds — namely, by the quality of its deep, sweet call — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening], though enclosed in the eggshell of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), with eyes covered by the darkness of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), surpasses all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — namely, by the quality of the call of dedicating and directing wholesome roots. Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a prince born that very moment to the chief queen of a <s>cakravartin</s> king — all the chief merchants, guild leaders, and district rulers pay homage to him — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening] — the world including the gods pays homage to him.

body.text: KP.85 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa ekaṃ vaiḍuryaṃ maṇiratnaṃ sumerumātraṃ rāśi kācamaṇikānabhibhavati evameva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhān abhibhavati / tatredamucyate 22
body.translated_text: KP.85 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a single <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) jewel the size of <s>Sumeru</s> would outshine a heap of glass jewels — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening] outshines all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// yathāpi vaiḍūryamaṇi prabhāsvaraḥ kācāmaṇīn abhibhavate prabhūtān /
imeva citte prathame bodhisattvo abhībhavati pṛthakcchrāvakān guṇān //
body.translated_text: Just as a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> jewel, radiant, outshines many glass jewels —

body.text: KP.86 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa rājño gramahiṣyāḥ tatkṣaṇajātaṃ kumāra sarvaśreṣṭhinaigamajānapadā koṭṭarājānaśca namasyanti / evameva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ sadevako loko namasyanti / tatredamucyate 23
body.translated_text: KP.86 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a prince born that very moment to the chief queen of a king — all the chief merchants, guild leaders, and district rulers pay homage to him — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening] — the world including the gods pays homage to him. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // yathāpi rājña pṛthivīśvarasya putro bhavellakṣaṇacitritāṅgaṃ

children.text: dṛṣtveva taṃ jātamātraṃ kumāraṃ sakoṭṭarājā praṇamanti paurāḥ
children.translated_text: upon seeing that prince, just born, the townspeople together with the district rulers bow down;

children.text: utpannamātre tathā bodhisatve sallakṣaṇaṃ taṃ jinarājaputraṃ
children.translated_text: even so, when a <s>bodhisattva</s> arises, that son of the king of <s>Jinas</s>, endowed with [auspicious] marks,

children.text: lokassadevo 'pi namaskaronti prasannacittaṃ bahumānapūrvaṃ //
children.translated_text: the world including the gods pays homage to him, with serene minds and filled with great respect.

body.translated_text: Just as for a king, the lord of the earth, a son is born with limbs adorned with [auspicious] marks —

body.text: KP.87 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa yāni himavantaḥ parvatarājā bhaiṣajyāni virohanti sarvānyamamānyaparigrahānyavikalpāni / yatra ca punarvyādhyā vyumpanāmyante taṃ vyādhiṃ praśamayanti / evameva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvo yajñānabhaiṣajyaṃ samudānayati tatsarva nirvikalpa samudānayati samacittatā sarvasattveṣu cikitsā prayati / tatredamucyate 24
body.translated_text: KP.87 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the medicines that grow on <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, are all without possessiveness, without appropriation, without conceptual distinction — and wherever diseases are applied [to them], they pacify that disease — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening], whatever medicine of knowledge he gathers, all of it he gathers without conceptual distinction, with equanimity of mind, administering treatment to all beings. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // himavanta ye paravatarāja bheṣajā rohanti te nirmamanirvikalpā /

children.text: yatropanāmyanti ca taṃ śamenti vyādhiṃ jarā cāpanayanti kecit
children.translated_text: wherever they are applied, they pacify that disease, and some remove old age;

children.text: jinātmajāpi samudānayanti yaṃ jñānabhaiṣajya vikalpa muktvā /
children.translated_text: so too the sons of the <s>Jina</s> gather the medicine of knowledge, having abandoned conceptual distinction;

children.text: hitārtha sarvaṃ samudānayanti samacitta sattveṣu cikitsa kurvan //
children.translated_text: they gather all for the benefit [of beings], with equanimity of mind, administering treatment to beings.

body.translated_text: The medicines that grow on <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, are without possessiveness and without conceptual distinction;

body.text: KP.88 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa navacandro namaskṛyate sā pūrṇacandro na tathā namaskṛyate / evameva kāśyapa ye mama śraddadhanti te balavantataraṃ bodhisattvaṃ namaskartavya / na tathāgata tatkasya heto bodhisattvanirjātā hi tathāgatāḥ tatredamucyate 25
body.translated_text: KP.88 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the new moon is venerated, but the full moon is not venerated in the same way — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, those who have faith in me should pay homage more strongly to a <s>bodhisattva</s>, not to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? Because <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise from <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// candraṃ navaṃ sarva namaskaronti tameva pūrṇaṃ na namaskaronti /
imeva yaḥ śraddadhatai jinātmajo sa bodhisattvaṃ namatā jinā na tu / //
body.translated_text:
Everyone venerates the new moon, but they do not venerate that same [moon when it is] full;
even so, whoever has faith in the son of the <s>Jina</s> should bow to the <s>bodhisattva</s>, not to the <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: KP.89 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa mātrikā sarvaśāstragrahaṇajñāne pūrvaṅgamā / evameva kāśyapa prathamacittotpādiko bodhisattvaḥ sarvabuddhavikurvitādhiṣṭhāne 'nuttare pūrvaṅgamaḥ //
body.translated_text: KP.89 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the alphabet (<s>mātṛkā</s>) is the prerequisite for the knowledge of grasping all sciences — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has just generated the first mind [of awakening] is the prerequisite for the unsurpassed miraculous transformations and empowerments of all <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: KP.90 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa na jātu kenaciccandramaṇḍalam utsṛjya tārakarūpaṃ namaskṛta pūrvaṃ / evameva kāśyapa na jātu paṇḍito mama śikṣāpratipanna bodhisattvaṃ riñcitvā śrāvakaṃ namaskaroti / tatredamucyate 26
body.translated_text: KP.90 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, no one ever, having abandoned the disc of the moon, would first pay homage to the form of a star — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, no wise person who follows my training, having forsaken a <s>bodhisattva</s>, would pay homage to a <s>śrāvaka</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// na kenaci candra vivarjayi tvā namaskṛtā tāragaṇā kadācit /
na jātu śikṣāpratipanna evaṃ mamātmajaṃ tyaja nameta śrāvakaḥ //
body.translated_text:
No one, having abandoned the moon, ever pays homage to the host of stars;
even so, one who follows the training, having forsaken my own son, would never bow to a <s>śrāvaka</s>.

body.text: KP.91 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa sadevako loko kācamaṇikasya parikarma kuryāt na jātu sa kācamaṇiko vaiḍūryamaṇiratno bhaviṣyati / evameva kāśyapa sarvaśīlaśikṣādhutaguṇasamādhisamanvāgato 'pi śrāvako na jātu sa bodhimaṇḍe niṣadyānuttarā samyaksambodhimabhisambotsyate / tatredamucyate 27
body.translated_text: KP.91 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, even if the world including the gods were to polish a glass jewel, that glass jewel would never become a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, even a <s>śrāvaka</s> endowed with all moral discipline, training, <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) would never sit at the seat of awakening and attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // yathāpi loko parikarma kuryās sadevakaḥ kācamaṇisya śuddhaye /

children.text: na kāca vaiḍūrya kadāci bheṣyate anyādṛśī tasya sadeva jātiḥ
children.translated_text: glass will never become <s>vaiḍūrya</s>; its birth is of a different nature, even with the gods;

children.text: evaṃ hi śīlāśrutaddhyānayukto yaḥ śrāvaka sarvaguṇānvito 'pi /
children.translated_text: even so, a <s>śrāvaka</s> endowed with moral conduct, learning, meditation, and all virtues,

children.text: na bodhimaṇḍasthita māra jitvā bodhiṃ spṛśitvā sugato bhaviṣyati //
children.translated_text: seated at the seat of awakening, having conquered <s>Māra</s>, will never touch awakening and become a <s>Sugata</s>.

body.translated_text: Just as the world including the gods might polish a glass jewel for its purification —

body.text: KP.92 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa vaiḍūryasya mahāmaṇiratnasya parikarma kriyamāṇairbahuṇām tatra karṣāpaṇaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhavati / evameva kāśyapa yatra bodhisattvasya parikarma kriyamāṇe bahūnāṃ tatra śrāvakapratyekabuddhaśatasahasrāṇām āyadvāraṃ bhavati / tatredamucyate 28
body.translated_text: KP.92 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, when a great <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem is being polished, it becomes the source of income for many hundreds of thousands of <s>karṣāpaṇas</s> (coins) — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva</s> is being cultivated, it becomes the source of income for many hundreds of thousands of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: // vaiḍūryaratne parikarmanīyante karṣāpaṇānāṃ ca bahu āyu bhoti /

children.text: buddhorasānāṃ parikarmaṇaṃ tathā āyo bahūnāṃ śrāvakānāṃ tatheva / 30 //
children.translated_text: even so, through the cultivation of the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, there arises income for the many <s>śrāvakas</s> likewise.

body.translated_text: When the <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem is being polished, there arises much income in <s>karṣāpaṇas</s>;

body.text: KP.93 atha khalu bhagavān punarevāyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapam āmantrayati sma / yasmiṃ kāśyapa deśe uṣṭradhūmaka kṛṣṇaśira uttānaśāyī bhavati sa deśa sopadravaḥ sopakleśa sopāyāso bhavati / sacetpuna kāśyapa yasmiṃ deśe bodhisattvo bhavati / sa deśa nirupadrava nirupakleśa nirupāyāso bhavati / tasmāttarhi kāśyapa sattvārthodyuktena bodhisattvena bhavitavyaṃ tena sarvakuśalamūlāni sarvasattvānām utsraṣṭavyaṃ / sarvaṃ ca kuśalamūla samyaksamudānayitavyaṃ / yaśca jñānabheṣajyaṃ paryeṣate tena caturdiśam gatvā sarvasattvānāṃ bhūtacikitsā kartavyāḥ bhūtacikitsāyā cca sattvā cikitsitavyāḥ
body.translated_text: KP.93 Then the Blessed One again addressed the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: In whatever region, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the camel-smoke-inhaler, the black-headed one, lies on his back — that region becomes afflicted with calamity, defilement, and distress. But, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in whatever region a <s>bodhisattva</s> dwells — that region becomes free from calamity, free from defilement, free from distress. Therefore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should be one who strives for the benefit of beings. By him, all roots of merit should be dedicated to all beings. And all roots of merit should be rightly gathered together. And he who seeks the medicine of knowledge (<s>jñānabhaiṣajya</s>) should go to the four directions and perform the true healing (<s>bhūtacikitsā</s>) of all beings; and beings should be healed through true healing.

body.text: KP.94 tatra kāśyapaḥ katamā bhūtacikitsāḥ yaduta rāgasya aśubhā cikitsā / dveṣasya maitrī cikitsāḥ mohasya pratītyasamutpādapratyavekṣaṇā cikitsāḥ sarvadṛṣṭīgatānāṃ śūnyatā cikitsāḥ sarvakalpavikalpaparikalpārambhaṇavitarkamanasīkārāṇām ānimitta cikitsāḥ sarvakāmadhāturūpadhātvārūpyadhātuprahāṇāyām apraṇihita cikitsāḥ sarvaviparyāsānā catvāro viparyāsa cikitsāḥ anitye nityasañjñāyāḥ anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārā iti cikitsāḥ duḥkhe sukhasañjñāyā duḥkhā sarvasaṃskārā iti cikitsāḥ anātmīye ātmīyasañjñāyā anātmāna sarvadharmā iti cikitsāḥ aśubhe śubhasañjñāyāḥ śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti cikitsāḥ
body.translated_text: KP.94 And what, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the true healing? Namely: for passion (<s>rāga</s>), the healing is contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>). For hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), the healing is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). For delusion (<s>moha</s>), the healing is contemplation of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). For all views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), the healing is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). For all conceptual elaboration, false imagination, proliferation, discursive thought, and mental attention — the healing is the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>). For the abandonment of all [attachment to] the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm — the healing is the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>). For all distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>), the healing is the four distortions: for the perception of permanence in what is impermanent — the healing is 'all conditioned things are impermanent.' For the perception of happiness in what is suffering — the healing is 'all conditioned things are suffering.' For the perception of self in what is without self — the healing is 'all <s>dharmas</s> are without self.' For the perception of beauty in what is impure — the healing is '<s>nirvāṇa</s> is peace.'

body.text: KP.95 catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni kāyevedanācittadharmasanniśritānāṃ cikitsāḥ kāye kāyānupasyī viharati na ca kāye kāyānupāśyanāyām ātmyadṛṣṭyāṃ patati / vedanāyāṃ vedanānupaśyī viharati na ca vedanānupaśyanāyā ātmadṛṣṭīgatena patati / citte cittānupaśyī viharati na ca cittānupaśyanāyāṃ jīvadiṣṭīye patati / dharme dharmānupaśyī viharati na ca dharmānupaśyanāyāṃ pudgaladṛṣṭīye patati / catvāri samyakprahāṇāni sarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇāya cikitsā / sarvakuśaladharmapāripūryaiḥ saṃvartante / catvāro dṛddhipādāḥ kāyacittapiṇḍagrāhotsargāya saṃvate / cikitsāḥ pañcendriyāṇi pañca balāni aśrādvyakausīdyamuṣitasmṛticittavikṣepaasamprajanyatāduṣprajñātācikitsāḥ sapta bodhyaṅgāni dharmasamūhājñānasya cikitsāḥ āryāṣṭāṅgo mārga dauṣprajñāsarvaparapravādināṃ kumārgapratipannānāṃ cikitsāḥ iyamucyate kāśyapa bhūtacikitsāḥ tatra kāśyapa bodhisattvena yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ
body.translated_text: KP.95 The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) are the healing for those attached to body, feeling, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>: one dwells contemplating the body in the body, yet does not fall into the view of self regarding the contemplation of body in the body. One dwells contemplating feeling in feeling, yet does not fall into the view of self regarding the contemplation of feeling. One dwells contemplating mind in mind, yet does not fall into the view of a living being regarding the contemplation of mind. One dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in <s>dharmas</s>, yet does not fall into the view of a person regarding the contemplation of <s>dharmas</s>. The four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>) are the healing for the abandonment of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; they conduce to the fulfillment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. The four bases of spiritual power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) conduce to the abandonment of attachment to body and mind. The healing of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) and five powers (<s>bala</s>) is for faithlessness, laziness, lost mindfulness, mental distraction, and lack of discernment and poor wisdom. The seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) are the healing for the heap of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge. The noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>) is the healing for those of poor wisdom, for all followers of other doctrines, and for those who have entered wrong paths. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called true healing. Therein, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should exert effort.

body.text: KP.96 yāvanta kāśyapa jāmbudvīpe vaidyā vā vaidyāntevāsino vā sarveṣāṃ teṣām jivako vaidyarājā agro mākhyāyate / yāvantaḥ kāśyapa trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sattvāḥ te sarve jīvakavaidyarājasadṛśā bhaveyuḥ te sarve paripṛccheran / dṛṣṭkaukṛtyapratiṣṭhitasya prapatitasya kiṃ bhaiṣajyam iti / te na samarthā na ca śaknoti tam artha ākhyātuṃ vā nirdeṣṭuṃ vā jñānavijñātā vā / tatra kāśyapa bodhisattvenaivam upaparikṣitavya na mayā lokikabhaiṣajyasantuṣṭirveditavyā / lokottara mayā jñānabhaiṣajyaṃ paryeṣṭitavyaṃ sarvakuśalamūlaṃ ca samyaksamudānayitavyam / mityevaṃ copaparīkṣitavyaḥ yacca jñānabhaiṣajyaṃ samudānayitvā tena caturdiśaṃ gatvā sarvasattvānāṃ bhūtacikitsā kartavyāḥ bhūtacikitsayā ca sattvāni cikitsitavyāḥ
body.translated_text: KP.96 However many physicians or physicians' apprentices there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, among all of them, <s>Jīvaka</s> the king of physicians is declared foremost. If, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, all beings in the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) were like <s>Jīvaka</s> the king of physicians, and all of them were asked: 'What is the medicine for one who is established in [wrong] views and remorse, one who has fallen?' — they would be unable and incapable of declaring, indicating, or making known that matter through knowledge. Therein, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should examine thus: 'I should not be content with worldly medicine. I should seek the supramundane medicine of knowledge, and I should rightly gather all roots of merit.' Having thus examined, and having gathered the medicine of knowledge, one should go to the four directions and perform the true healing of all beings; and beings should be healed through true healing.

body.text: KP.97 tatra kataraṃ lokottaraṃ jñānabhaiṣajyaṃ / yadidaṃ hetupratyayajñānaḥ nairātmyeniḥsattvaḥnirjīvaniṣpoṣanīṣpudgaleṣu dharmeṣvadhimuktijñānaṃ / śūnyatānupalambheṣu dharmeṣu anutrāsaḥ cittaparigaveṣatāye vīryaṃ / sa evaṃ cittaṃ parigaveṣate / kataraṃ cittaṃ rajyati vā duṣyati vā muhyati vā / atītaṃ vā anāgataṃ vā pratyutpannaṃ vā / yadi tāvad atītaṃ cittaṃ tatkṣīṇaṃ / yādanāgataṃ cittaṃ tadasamprāptaḥ atha pratyutpannasya cittasya sthitirnāsti /
body.translated_text: KP.97 And what is the supramundane medicine of knowledge? It is the knowledge of causes and conditions (<s>hetupratyayajñāna</s>); the knowledge of conviction regarding <s>dharmas</s> that are without self (<s>nairātmya</s>), without a being (<s>niḥsattva</s>), without a life-principle (<s>nirjīva</s>), without a nourisher (<s>niṣpoṣa</s>), without a person (<s>niṣpudgala</s>); fearlessness regarding <s>dharmas</s> that are empty and unapprehensible; and vigor in the investigation of mind. One investigates the mind thus: Which mind becomes passionate, or hateful, or deluded? Is it the past, or the future, or the present? If the past mind — that has ceased. If the future mind — that has not yet arrived. And for the present mind, there is no abiding.

body.text: KP.98 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa na bahirdhā nobhayāyomantarāle upalabhyate / cittaṃ hi kāśyapa arūpyanidarśanam apratigham anābhāsam avijñāptikam apratiṣṭhitam aniketaḥ cittaṃ hi kāśyapa sarvabuddhairna dṛṣṭaṃ na paśyanti na paśyiṣyanti na drakṣyanti yatsarvabuddhairna dṛṣtaṃ na paśyanti na drakṣyanti kīdṛśastasya pracāro draṣṭavyaṃ nānyatra vitathaviparyāsapatitāyā santatyā dharmāḥ pravartante 3 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa māyāsadṛśamm abhūtaṃ vikalpya vividhopapattiṃ parigṛhṇāti 4 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa vāyusadṛśaṃ dūraṅgamam agrāhyam apracāra 5 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa nadīsrotasadṛśamm anavastitam utpannaṃ bhagnavilīna 6 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa pradīpārciḥsadṛśaṃ hetupratyayatayā pravartate / jvalati ca 7
body.translated_text: KP.98 For the mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is not to be found outside, nor inside, nor in between the two. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is formless, without appearance, without resistance, without manifestation, inexpressible, unsupported, without abode. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, has not been seen, is not seen, and will not be seen by all the <s>Buddhas</s>. What has not been seen, is not seen, and will not be seen by all the <s>Buddhas</s> — of what nature is its activity to be understood, except that <s>dharmas</s> proceed from a continuum fallen into false distortion? 3. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like an illusion — imagining what is unreal, it grasps various forms of rebirth. 4. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like the wind — far-ranging, ungraspable, without a sphere of activity. 5. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a river's current — unstable, once arisen it is broken and dissolved. 6. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like the flame of a lamp — it operates through the condition of causes and conditions, and it burns. 7

body.text: KP.99 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa vidyusadṛśa kṣaṇabhaṅgāvyavasthitaṃ 8 / cittaṃ hi kāśyapa ākāśasadṛśam āgantukerupakleśe saṅkiśyate 9 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa vānarasadṛśa viṣayābhilāṣi vicitrakarmasaṃsthānatayā 10 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa citrakārsadṛśa vicitrakarmābhisaṃskaraṇatayā / 11 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa anavasthitaṃ nānākleśapravartanatayā cittaṃ hi kāśyapa ekacaram advitīyacittābhisandhānatayā 13 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa rājasadṛśaṃ sarvadharmādhipateyā 14 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa amitrasadṛśaṃ sarvaduḥkhasañjananatayā 15
body.translated_text: KP.99 The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like lightning — unstable, breaking apart in an instant. 8. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like space — it is defiled by adventitious defilements. 9. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a monkey — desirous of sense objects, by virtue of its variegated activity. 10. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a painter — by virtue of its fashioning variegated <s>karmic</s> formations. 11. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is unstable — by virtue of its operating through various defilements. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, wanders alone — by virtue of its engaging with a single, non-dual mind. 13. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a king — by virtue of its sovereignty over all <s>dharmas</s>. 14. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like an enemy — by virtue of its generating all suffering. 15

body.text: KP.100 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa pāṃsvāgārasadṛśam anitye nityasañjñayā 16 cittam hi kāśyapa nīlamakṣikāsadṛśam aśuco śucisañjñāyā 17 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa matsyabaḍīśasadṛśa duḥkhe sukhasañjñāyā 18 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa svapnasadṛśam anātmīye ātmīyasañjñāyā 19 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa pratyarthikasadṛśam vividhakāraṇākaraṇatayā 20 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa ojāhārayakṣasadṛśa sadāvatāragaveṣaṇatayā 21 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa arisadṛśaṃ sadā cchidrārāmagaveṣaṇatayā 22
body.translated_text: KP.100 The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a dusty house — by virtue of perceiving permanence in the impermanent. 16. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a blowfly — by virtue of perceiving purity in the impure. 17. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a fish-hook — by virtue of perceiving happiness in suffering. 18. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a dream — by virtue of perceiving self in what is without self. 19. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like an adversary — by virtue of creating various causes [of harm]. 20. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a vitality-devouring <s>yakṣa</s> — by virtue of always seeking an opening [to attack]. 21. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a foe — by virtue of always seeking delight in vulnerabilities. 22

body.text: KP.101 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa sadā unnatāvanatam anunayapratighopahataṃ 23 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa corasadṛśa sarvakuśalamūlamuṣaṇatayā 24 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa rūpārāma pagataṅganetrasadṛśaṃ 25 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa śabdārāma saṅgrāmabherīsadṛśa 26 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa sadā gandhārāma varāha iva mīḍakuṇape 27 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa rasārāma rasabhojyaceṭīsadṛśaṃ 28 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa sparṣārāma makṣikeva tailapātre 29
body.translated_text: KP.101 The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is always rising and falling, afflicted by attraction and aversion. 23. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is like a thief — by virtue of stealing all roots of merit. 24. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, delights in form — like the eyes of [...]. 25. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, delights in sound — like a battle drum. 26. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, always delights in smell — like a boar in filth and carcasses. 27. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, delights in taste — like a slave devoted to tasty food. 28. The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, delights in touch — like a fly in an oil vessel. 29

body.text: KP.102 cittaṃ hi kāśyapa parigaveṣamaṇaṃ na labhyate 30 yanna labhyate tannopalabhyate tannātītaṃ nānāgataṃ na pratyutpannaṃ / yannātītaṃ nānāgataṃ na pratyutpannaṃ tatradhvasamatikrāntaṃ yatryadhvasamatikrāntaṃ / tannaivāsti neva nāsti / yannaivāsti na nāsti / tadajātaṃ yadajātaṃ / tasya nāsti svabhāvaḥ yasya nāsti svabhāvaḥ tasya nāstyutpāda / yasya nāstyutpādaḥ tasya nāsti nirodhaḥ yasya nāsti nirodhaḥ tasya nāsti vigamaḥ avigamastasyarna gatirnāgatirna cyutirnopapattiḥ yatra na gatirnāgatirna cyutirnopapattiḥ tatra na kecit saṃskārāḥ yatra na kecit saṃskārāḥ tadasaṃskṛtaṃ / tadāryāṇāṃ gotra
body.translated_text: KP.102 The mind, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, when investigated, is not to be found. 30. What is not found is not apprehended. What is not apprehended is neither past, nor future, nor present. What is neither past, nor future, nor present has transcended the three times. What has transcended the three times neither exists nor does not exist. What neither exists nor does not exist is unborn. What is unborn has no own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). What has no own-nature has no arising. What has no arising has no cessation. What has no cessation has no passing away. For what has no passing away, there is no going, no coming, no passing away, no rebirth. Where there is no going, no coming, no passing away, no rebirth — there are no conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>). Where there are no conditioned formations, that is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). That is the lineage of the noble ones (<s>ārya</s>).

body.text: KP.103 ya 1 āryāṇāṃ gotra / tatrarna śikṣā na niśrayo nāniśrayaḥ yatra na śikṣā na niḥśrayo nāniśrayaḥ tatra na śikṣāvyatikramaḥ yatra na śikṣāvyatikramaḥ tatra na saṃvaro nāsaṃvaraḥ yatra na saṃvaro nāsaṃvara / tatra na cāro nācāraḥ na pracāraḥ yatra na cāro nācāra na pracāraḥ tatra na cittaṃ na cetasikā dharmāḥ yatra na cittaṃ na cetasikā dharmāḥ tatra na mano na vijñānaḥ yatra na mano na vijñāna / tatra na karmo na vipākaḥ yatra na karmo na vipākaḥ tatra na sukhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ yatra na sukhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ tadāryāṇāṃ gotraṃ yadāryānāṃ gotraṃ tatra na karmo na karmābhisaṃskāro nāpi tatra gotre kāyena karma kṛyate na vācā na manasā / nāpi tatra gotre hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamavyavasthānaṃ samaṃ tadgotram ākāśasamatayā / nirviśeṣaṃ tadgotraṃ sarvadharmaikarasatayā /
body.translated_text: KP.103 [...] the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) of the noble ones. Therein there is no training, no reliance, and no non-reliance. Where there is no training, no reliance, and no non-reliance, there is no transgression of training. Where there is no transgression of training, there is neither restraint nor non-restraint. Where there is neither restraint nor non-restraint, there is no conduct, no non-conduct, and no course of action. Where there is no conduct, no non-conduct, and no course of action, there is no mind and no mental factors. Where there is no mind and no mental factors, there is no <s>manas</s> (mentation) and no <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Where there is no <s>manas</s> and no <s>vijñāna</s>, there is no <s>karma</s> (action) and no <s>vipāka</s> (fruition). Where there is no <s>karma</s> and no <s>vipāka</s>, there is no pleasure and no suffering. Where there is no pleasure and no suffering — that is the <s>gotra</s> of the noble ones. In that <s>gotra</s> of the noble ones, there is no <s>karma</s> and no volitional formation of <s>karma</s>; nor in that <s>gotra</s> is <s>karma</s> performed by body, speech, or mind. Nor in that <s>gotra</s> is there a determination of inferior, superior, or middling — that <s>gotra</s> is equal, through its equality with space. That <s>gotra</s> is without distinction, through the one taste of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: KP.104 viviktaṃ tadgotraṃ kāyacittavivekatayā / anulomaṃ tadgotraṃ nirvāṇasya / vimalaṃ tadgotraṃ sarvakleśamalavigata amamaṃ tadgotram ahaṅkāramamakāravigataṃ / aviṣamaṃ tadgotraṃ bhūtābhūtasamatayā niryātaṃ satyaṃ tadgotraṃ paramārthasatyayā / akṣayaṃ tadgotra atyantatānutpannaṃ / nityaṃ tadgotraṃ sadā dharmatathatayā / aśubhaṃ tadgotraṃ nirvāṇaparamatayā / śubhaṃ tadgotraṃ sarvākāramalavigataṃ / anātmā tadgotram ātmanaḥ parigaveṣyamāṇanupalambhāt / viśuddhaṃ tadgotram atyantaviśuddhatayā //
body.translated_text: KP.104 That <s>gotra</s> is secluded, through the seclusion of body and mind. That <s>gotra</s> is in conformity with <s>nirvāṇa</s>. That <s>gotra</s> is stainless, free from the stain of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). That <s>gotra</s> is without possessiveness, free from the conceit of 'I' and 'mine.' That <s>gotra</s> is even, through the equality of the real and the unreal. That <s>gotra</s> is true, through ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). That <s>gotra</s> is inexhaustible, being absolutely unarisen. That <s>gotra</s> is permanent, through the perpetual suchness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatathatā</s>). That <s>gotra</s> is impure [in the sense of being beyond worldly purity], through the supremacy of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. That <s>gotra</s> is pure, free from stain in all aspects. That <s>gotra</s> is without self (<s>anātman</s>), because the self is not found when sought. That <s>gotra</s> is purified, through absolute purity.

body.text: KP.105 adhyātmaṃ kāśyapa parimargatha mā bahirvidhāvadhvaṃ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ bhaviṣyanti kāśyapa anāgate dhvani bhikṣavaḥ śvaloṣṭvānujavanasadṛśāḥ kathaṃ ca kāśyapa bhikṣavaḥ śvaloṣṭānujavanasadṛśā bhavati / tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa śvāno loṣṭunā trāsitaḥ tameva loṣṭuranudhāvati / na tamanudhāvati / yena sa loṣṭuṃ kṣiptaṃ bhavati / evameva kāśyapa satyeke śramaṇabrāhmaṇā ye rūpaśabdagandharasasparśairbhayabhītā araṇyāyataneṣu viharanti / teṣā tatrekākinām advitīyānāṃ kāyapraviviktavihāriṇāṃ rajanīyāstajjakriyā rupaśabdagandharasasparśāvabhāsam āgacchanti / te tatrāvekṣakāḥ sukhalikānuyogam anuyuktā viharanti ranti /
body.translated_text: KP.105 <s>Kāśyapa</s>, seek inwardly; do not run outward. Why? Because in the future, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, there will be monks who are like dogs chasing clods of earth. And how, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are monks like dogs chasing clods of earth? Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a dog that is startled by a clod of earth chases after that very clod — it does not chase after the one who threw the clod. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, there are certain <s>śramaṇas</s> (renunciants) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who, frightened by forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles, dwell in forest retreats. Yet for those who dwell alone there, solitary and without a second, practicing seclusion of body, the enticing, associated appearances of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles come to them. They, being observers there, dwell indulging in the pursuit of pleasure.

body.text: KP.106 te na jāna jānanti na buddhyanti kiṃ rūpāśabdagandharasasparśāna nīḥsaraṇam iti / te ajānantaḥ abuddhyantaḥ teṣāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasasparśānāsvādaṃ cādīnavaṃ cā niḥsaraṇaṃ ca avatīrṇā grāmanagaranigamarāṣarājadhāniṣva punareva rūpaśabdagandharasasparśarhannyaṃ saced araṇyagatā kālaṃ kurvanti / teṣāṃ lokikasaṃvarasthitānā svargaloke upapattirbhavati / te tatrāpi divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇairhanyaṃ / te tataścyutā aparimuktā samānāścaturbhirapāyairnirayatiryag niyamalokāsuraiḥ evaṃ hi kāśyapa bhikṣavaḥ śvaloṣṭvanujavanasadṛśā bhavanti / //
body.translated_text: KP.106 They do not know, they do not understand: what is the escape from forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles? Not knowing, not understanding the enjoyment, the danger, and the escape from those forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles, they descend into villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and capital cities, and once again [indulge in] forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles. Even if they have gone to the forest, they die [there in vain]. For those established in worldly restraint, there is rebirth in the heavenly world. Even there they are afflicted by the five strands of divine sense-pleasure. Having fallen from there, still not liberated, [they encounter] the four lower realms — hell, animal birth, the world of <s>Yama</s>, and the <s>asuras</s> (titans). Thus indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, monks become like dogs chasing clods of earth.

body.text: KP.107 katham ca kāśyapa bhikṣurna śvaloṣṭvanujavanasadṛśo bhavati yaḥ kāśyapa bhikṣu ākruṣṭo na pratyākrośati tāḍito na pratitāḍayati paṃsito na pratipaṃsayati / bhaṇḍito na pratibhaṇḍayati / roṣito na pratiroṣayati / ādhyātmaṃ cittaniddhyaptiṃ pratyavekṣate / ko vākruṣṭo vā tāḍito vā / paṃsito vā bhaṇḍito vā roṣito vā / evaṃ hi kāśyapa bhikṣurna śvaloṣṭvanujavanasadṛśo bhavanasadṛśo bhavati / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.107 And how, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a monk not like a dog chasing clods of earth? The monk, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who, when abused, does not abuse in return; when struck, does not strike back; when reviled, does not revile in return; when quarreled with, does not quarrel back; when angered, does not respond with anger — he investigates inwardly, contemplating the mind: who is abused, or struck, or reviled, or quarreled with, or angered? Thus indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a monk is not like a dog chasing clods of earth. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
śvāno yathā loṣṭuna trāsyamāno
anudhāvate loṣṭu na yena kṣiptaṃ
em evihekai śramaṇā dvijā vā
rūpādibhītā vanavāsam āśritā /
// teṣāṃ ca tasmin vasatām araṇye
rūpādayo daśanam eta iṣṭā /
upekṣakādhyātmagate nabhijñā
ādīnavān niḥsaraṇeḥkam eṣā
ajānamānā puna grāmam āśritā /
punepi rūpehi vihanyamānā
śyutaśca devai manujaiśca kecit
tatrāpi divyān upabhujya bhogā 3
apāyabhūmiḥ prapatanti kecit cyutā cyutā duḥkhamupaiti mūḍhāḥ

children.text: evaṃ hi te duḥkhaśatānubaddhā śvaloṣṭatulyā sugatena deśitā / 4
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, bound by hundreds of sufferings, they have been declared by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) to be like dogs chasing clods.

children.text:
ākruṣṭa nākrośati tāḍitastathā na paṃsitaḥ paṃsayateśca kecit
na bhaṇḍito bhaṇḍayate tathānyān aroṣito roṣayate ca sūrataḥ 5
adhyātmacittaṃ pratiprakṣataśca gaveṣate śāntatavi smṛtīmān
evaṃvidhaḥ śīlavratopapaṇnoḥ na śvānatulya kathito jinena / 6 //
children.translated_text: One endowed with such moral conduct and observances is not declared by the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) to be like a dog.

body.translated_text:
Just as a dog, when startled by a clod of earth, chases after the clod and not the one who threw it —
even so here, certain <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, frightened by forms and the like, resort to forest dwelling.
But for those dwelling in that forest, the desired forms and the like come as appearances.
Those who are mere observers, not knowing the inward [path], not understanding the danger and the escape from these,
not knowing, they resort again to the village;
again afflicted by forms and the like,
some, having fallen from among gods and humans,
having enjoyed divine pleasures there too,
some fall into the lower realms — the deluded, dying and dying again, encounter suffering.

body.text: KP.108 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa kuśalo aśvadamaka suto / yatra yatra pṛthivīpradeśe aśva skhalati / utkumbhati vā khaḍuṅkakriyā vā karoti / tatra tatra caiva pṛthivīpradeśe nigṛhṇāti sa tathā tathā nigṛhṇāti yanna punarapi na prakupyate / evameva kāśyapa yogācāro bhikṣuryatrayatraivaṃ cittasya vikāraṃ paśyati / tatra tatraivāsya nigrahāya pratipadyate / sa tathā tathā cittaṃ nigṛhṇāti yathā na puna prakupyate tatredamucyate / //
body.translated_text: KP.108 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a skilled trainer of horses — wherever on the ground the horse stumbles, rears up, or behaves stubbornly, right there on that very spot he restrains it. He restrains it in such a way that it does not act up again. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a monk practicing <s>yoga</s> — wherever he sees a disturbance of the mind, right there he undertakes to restrain it. He restrains the mind in such a way that it does not become agitated again. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
yathāśvasūta kuśalo bhaveta skhalitaṃ ca aśva samabhigr. hat. /
yogī tathā cittavikāra dṛṣṭvā tathā nigṛhṇāti yathā na kupyate / //
body.translated_text:
Just as a skilled horse trainer, when the horse stumbles, would restrain it,
so the <s>yogī</s>, having seen a disturbance of mind, restrains it so that it does not become agitated.

body.text: KP.109 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa galagraha sarvendriyāṇāṃ graho bhavati jīvitendriyasyoparodhe vartate / evameva kāśyapa sarvadṛṣṭigatānāmmātmagrāho dharmajīvitendriyasyoparodhena vartate / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.109 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a throat-seizing disease (<s>galagraha</s>) seizes all the sense faculties and obstructs the life faculty. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, among all those who have fallen into views, the grasping of self obstructs the life faculty of the <s>Dharma</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: galagraho ve yatha jīvitendriyā nigṛhṇate nāsya sukhaṃ dadāti /
children.translated_text: Just as a throat-seizing disease seizes the life faculty and gives no comfort,

children.text: dṛṣṭikṛtānāmapi ātmadṛṣṭi vināśayeta ima dharmajīvitaṃ //
children.translated_text: so too, the self-view of those who have fallen into views destroys this <s>Dharma</s>-life.

body.text: KP.110 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa puruṣo yato yataḥ baddho bhavati tatastata eva mocayitavyo bhavati / evameva kāśyapa yato yata eva cittaṃ sajyati / tatastata eva mocayitavyaṃ bhavati / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.110 It is as if, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a man who is bound — wherever he is bound, from that very place he must be freed. Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, wherever the mind becomes attached, from that very place it must be freed. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
yathāpi baddhaḥ puruṣaḥ samantāt samantato mocayitavya bhoti
evaṃ yahīm sajjati mūḍhacittaṃ tatastato yogina mocanīyam //
body.translated_text:
Just as a man who is bound on all sides must be freed from all sides,
even so, wherever the deluded mind becomes attached, from there the <s>yogin</s> must free it.

body.text:
KP.111 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasyākāśapaligodhau / katamau dvau /
lokāyatamantraparyeṣṭitā ca / utsadapātracīvaradhāraṇatayā ca / imau dvau / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.111 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, two things that are like [obstructions in] the sky for a renunciant. Which two? The pursuit of <s>Lokāyata</s> (worldly philosophy) and mantras, and the wearing of bowl and robes for the sake of mere livelihood. These are the two. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: lokāyatasyābhyasanābhiyogo tatotsadaṃ cīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: The zealous pursuit and study of <s>Lokāyata</s>, and the wearing of robes and carrying of bowl for mere livelihood —

children.text: ākāśabodhe imi dve pratiṣṭhite tau bodhisattvena vivarjanīyau //
children.translated_text: these two are established as obstructions [like those of] the sky for a <s>bodhisattva</s>, and should be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: KP.112 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya gāḍhabandhano / katamau dviyadutātmadṛṣṭikṛtabandhanaṃ ca lābhasatkāraślokabandhanaṃ cetīme kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya gāḍhabandhanaṃ / tatredamucyate 2 //
body.translated_text: KP.112 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, two firm bonds of a renunciant. Which two? The bond of the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), and the bond of gain, honor, and fame. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two firm bonds of a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
dve bandhane pravrajitasya gāḍhe dṛṣṭikṛtaṃ bandhanam uktam ādaiḥ
satkāralābho yaśabandhanaṃ ca te sarvadā pravrajitena tyajye //
body.translated_text: Two bonds of a renunciant are firm: the bond of views has been declared by the ancients, and the bond of gain, honor, and fame — both should always be abandoned by the renunciant.

body.text: KP.113 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasyāntārayakaro dharmau / katamo dvau /

children.text: gṛhapatipakṣasevanā ca āryapakṣavidveṣaṇatā cetīme kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasyāntarāyakarau dharmau / tatredamucyate 3 //
children.translated_text: Associating with the party of householders, and hostility toward the party of noble ones — these, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two obstructive <s>dharmas</s> for a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

body.translated_text: KP.113 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, two obstructive <s>dharmas</s> for a renunciant. Which two?

children.text: gṛhasthapakṣasya ca sevanā yā ācāryapakṣasya ca yā vigarhaṇā /
children.translated_text: The association with the party of householders, and the censuring of the party of teachers —

children.text: dvāvantarāyo paripanthabhūto tau bodhisattvena vivaryanīyo //
children.translated_text: these two are obstacles that stand as hindrances, and should be avoided by the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: KP.114 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya malau katamau dvan / yaduta kleṣādhivāsanatā ca mitrakulabhekṣākakulādvyavasanatāgrahaṇaṃ cetime kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya malo / tatredamucyate // 4 //
body.translated_text: KP.114 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, two impurities of a renunciant. Which two? Namely, harboring <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and the attachment to and reliance upon benefactor families for the sake of alms. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two impurities of a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: kleśaśca yo pravrajito dhivāsayet mitraṃ sa bhekṣākakulaṃ ca sevati /
children.translated_text: A renunciant who harbors <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and frequents friends and alms-giving families —

children.text: etau jinendreṇa hi deśitau malo tau bodhisattvena vivarjanīyoḥ //
children.translated_text: These two stains have been taught by the lord of <s>Jinas</s>; they should be avoided by the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: KP.115 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasyāśaniprapātau / katamau dvau / saddharmapratikṣepaśca cyutaśīlasya ca śraddhādeyaparibhogaṃ cetīme kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya aśanīprapāto dharmaḥ tatredamucyate // 5 //
body.translated_text: KP.115 These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are two thunderbolts for a renunciant. Which two? The rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and the enjoyment of food offered in faith by one who has fallen from moral conduct. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two thunderbolts for a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: saddharmasya pratikṣepa śyutaśīlasya bhojanaṃ /
children.translated_text: The rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and the eating [of food] by one fallen from moral conduct —

children.text: aśaniprapāto dvāvetau varjanīyo nṛpātmakaiḥ //
children.translated_text: these are the two thunderbolts, to be avoided by the sons of the king.

body.text: KP.116 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya vraṇau katamau dvau / paradau pratyavekṣanatā ca svadauṣapraticchādanatā cetīme kāśyapa dvau pravrajita vraṇau tatredamucyate 16 //
body.translated_text: KP.116 These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are two wounds of a renunciant. Which two? Scrutinizing the faults of others and concealing one's own faults. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two wounds of a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: vṛṇute ca svakā dauṣā paridoṣāśca vīkṣate /
children.translated_text: One conceals one's own faults and scrutinizes the faults of others —

children.text: viṣāgnitulyo dvāvetau vraṇau tyajyau parikṣakaiḥ //
children.translated_text: like poison and fire, these two wounds should be abandoned by the discerning.

body.text: KP.117 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya paridāgho katamo dvau / yaduta sakāṣāyasya ca kāṣāyadhāraṇaṃ śīlavantā guṇavantā cāntikādupasthānaparicaryāsvīkaraṇaṃ cetīme kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya paridāgho / tatredamucyate 7 //
body.translated_text: KP.117 These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are two fevers of a renunciant. Which two? Namely, wearing the <s>kāṣāya</s> (ochre robe) while having defilements in one's heart, and accepting the service and attendance of those who are virtuous and endowed with good qualities. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two fevers of a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text: sakaṣāyacittasya kāṣāyadhāraṇaṃ śīlānvitānāṃ ca sakāśa sevanā paricaryupasthānabhivādanaṃ ca dharmāvimau dvau parivarjaṇīyā //
body.translated_text: Wearing the <s>kāṣāya</s> robe with a defiled mind, and serving in the company of those endowed with moral conduct, accepting their attendance and salutations — these two <s>dharmas</s> should be avoided.

body.text: KP.118 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya dīrghaglānyau katamau dvau / yad abhimānikasya ca cittanidhyaptirmahāyānasamprasthitānāṃ sattvānā vicchandanā ime kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya dīrghagailā / tatredamucyate 18 //
body.translated_text: KP.118 These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are two chronic illnesses of a renunciant. Which two? Namely, the mental obsession of one who is arrogant, and discouraging beings who have set out on the <s>mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle). These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two chronic illnesses of a renunciant. Regarding this, it is said:

children.text: nidhyapti cittasyabhimānikānāṃ vicchandanāyāpi ca buddhayānaṃ /
children.translated_text: The mental obsession of the arrogant, and discouraging [beings from] the <s>buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle) —

children.text: ime hi dve pravrajitasya glānye ukte jinenāpratipudgalena //
children.translated_text: these two have been declared chronic illnesses of a renunciant by the <s>Jina</s>, the incomparable being.

body.text: KP.119 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya acikitso gailānyau / katamau dvau /

children.text: yādutābhīkṣṇāpattiāpadyanatā / avyutthānatā ceti ime kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya acikitso glānyo 9 //
children.translated_text: Namely, repeatedly falling into transgressions, and not rising [from them]. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two incurable illnesses of a renunciant.

body.translated_text: KP.119 These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are two incurable illnesses of a renunciant. Which two?

body.text:
KP.120 dvāvimau kāśyapa pravrajitasya śalyo katamau dvau / yaduta śikṣāpadasamatikramaṃ ca anādattasārasya ca kālakriyā ime kāśyapa dvau pravrajitasya śalyo 10
//
body.translated_text: KP.120 These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are two thorns of a renunciant. Which two? Namely, transgressing the rules of training, and dying without having grasped the essence [of the teaching]. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the two thorns of a renunciant.

body.text: KP.121 śramaṇa śramaṇa iti kāśyapa ucyate / kiyannu tāvat kāśyapa śramaṇaḥ śramaṇa ityucyate / catvāra ime kāśyapa śramaṇaḥ katame catvāraḥ yaduta varṇarūpaliṅgasaṃsthānaśramaṇa / ācāraguptikuhakaśramaṇaḥ kīrtiśabdaślokaśramaṇaḥ bhūtapratipattiśramaṇaḥ ime kāśyapa catvāraḥ śramaṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: KP.121 '<s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>śramaṇa</s>' (renunciant), <s>Kāśyapa</s>, it is said. To what extent, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a <s>śramaṇa</s> called a '<s>śramaṇa</s>'? There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four [types of] <s>śramaṇas</s>. What are the four? Namely, the <s>śramaṇa</s> by outward appearance, color, marks, and form; the <s>śramaṇa</s> of guarded conduct and deceit; the <s>śramaṇa</s> of fame, renown, and reputation; and the <s>śramaṇa</s> of genuine practice. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>śramaṇas</s>.

body.text: KP.122 tatra kāśyapa katamo varṇarūpaliṅgasaṃsthānaśramaṇaḥ iha kāśyapa ihekatyaśramaṇa varaṇarupaliṅgasaṃsthānasamanvāgato bhavati / saṅghāṭīpariveṣṭhito muṇḍaśiraḥ supātrapāṇaiḥ parigṛhītaḥ sa ca bhavatyapariśuddhakāyakarmasamudācāra apariśuddhavākkarmasamudācāraḥ apariśuddhamanaskarmasamudācārauḥ bhavati / ayukta amuktaḥ adāntaḥ aśāntaḥ aguptaḥ avinitaḥ lubdhaḥ alasoḥ duḥśīlappāpadharmasamācāraḥ ayamucyate kāśyapa varṇarūpaliṅgasaṃsthānaśramaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: KP.122 Now, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who is the <s>śramaṇa</s> by outward appearance, color, marks, and form? Here, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain <s>śramaṇa</s> is endowed with the [proper] color, appearance, marks, and form of a renunciant — wrapped in the <s>saṅghāṭī</s> (outer robe), with shaven head, holding a bowl in hand. Yet his conduct of body is impure, his conduct of speech is impure, his conduct of mind is impure. He is undisciplined, unrestrained, untamed, unpeaceful, unguarded, untrained, greedy, lazy, of bad moral conduct and evil practices. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the <s>śramaṇa</s> by outward appearance, color, marks, and form.

body.text: KP.123 tatra kāśyapa katamaḥ ācāraguptikuhakaḥ śramaṇaḥ iha kāśyapa ihaikatyaśramaṇaḥ ācāracāritrasampano bhavati samprajānacārī caturbhi īryāpathairlūhānnapānabhojī santuṣṭaḥ caturbhirāryavaṃśerasaṃsṛṣṭo gṛhasthapravrajitairalpabhāṣyo 'lpamantraḥ te cāsyeryāpathāḥ kuhanalapanatayā kalpitā bhavanti / na cittapariśuddhaye / na śamāya nopaśamāya / na damāya / upalambhadṛṣṭikaśca bhavati / śūnyatānupalambhāśca dharmesu śrutvā prapātasañjñī bhavati / śūnyatāvādināṃ ca bhikṣuṇām antike aprasādasañjñim utpādayati iyam ucyate kāśyapa ācāraguptikuhaka śramaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: KP.123 Now, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who is the <s>śramaṇa</s> of guarded conduct and deceit? Here, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain <s>śramaṇa</s> is accomplished in conduct and deportment, acting with full awareness in the four postures, eating coarse food and drink, content with the four <s>āryavaṃśas</s> (noble lineages), unmingled with householders and renunciants, of few words and few conversations. Yet his deportments are contrived through deceit and pretense — not for the purification of mind, not for calm, not for tranquility, not for taming. He holds the view of apprehension. And upon hearing that <s>dharmas</s> are empty and unapprehensible, he has the perception of falling into an abyss. And he generates the perception of displeasure toward those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) who teach emptiness. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the <s>śramaṇa</s> of guarded conduct and deceit.

body.text: KP.124 tatra kāśyapa katamaḥ kīrtiśabdaślokaḥ śramaṇaḥ iha kāśyapa ihaikatyaśramaṇaḥ pratisaṅkhyāya śīlaṃ rakṣati / kathamān pare jānīyurśīlavatān iti / pratisaṅkhyāya śrutam udgṛhṇīte kathamāṃ pare jānīyurbahuśruta iti / pratisaṅkhyāyāraṇye prativasati / kathamāṃ pare jānīyu āraṇyaka iti / pratisaṅkhyāya alpecchaḥ santuṣṭaḥ pravivikto viharat / yāvad eva paropadarśanāya na nirvedāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya nopaśamāya / nā sambodhaye / na śrāmaṇyāya / na brāhmaṇāya / na nirvāṇāya / ayamucyate kāśyapa kīrtiśabdaślokaśramaṇa //
body.translated_text: KP.124 Now, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who is the <s>śramaṇa</s> of fame, renown, and reputation? Here, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain <s>śramaṇa</s> guards his moral conduct with the thought: 'How might others know me as virtuous?' He takes up learning with the thought: 'How might others know me as learned?' He dwells in the forest with the thought: 'How might others know me as a forest-dweller?' He lives with few desires, content, in seclusion — all merely for the display to others, not for disenchantment, not for dispassion, not for cessation, not for tranquility, not for full awakening, not for the life of a <s>śramaṇa</s>, not for the holy life, not for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the <s>śramaṇa</s> of fame, renown, and reputation.

body.text: KP.125 tatra kāśyapa katamo bhūtapratipattiḥ śramaṇaḥ yaḥ kāśyapa bhikṣuranarthiko bhavati kāyena ca jīvitenāpi / kaḥ punarvvādo lābhasatkāraśloke / śūnyatā ānimittā apraṇihitāśca dhrmāṃ śrutvā āptamano bhavati tathatvatāyāṃ pratipanno nirvāṇe cāpyanarthikā brahmacaryaṃ carati / kaḥ punarvādastraidhātukābhinandanatayā śūnyatādṛṣṭyāpyanarthiko bhavati / kaḥ punarvāda ātmasattvajīvapauṣapudgaladṛṣṭyā / dharmapratisaraṇaśca bhavati / kleṣānāṃ ca adhyātmavimokṣamargati / na bahirdhā dhāvati atyantapariśuddhāśca prakṛtyā sarvadharmā asaṅkliṣṭān paśyati / ātmadvīpaśca bhavatyananyadvīpaḥ dharmato 'pi tathāgataṃ na samanupaśyati kaḥ punarvāda rūpakāyena / virāgato 'pi dharmaṃ nābhiniviśate kaḥ punarvāda uta vākpathodāharaṇena / asaṃskṛtamapi cāryasaṅghaṃ na vikalpayati / kaḥ punarvādo gaṇasaṃ nipātataḥ nāpi kasyaciddharmasya prarhāṇāyābhiyukto bhavati na bhāvanāyairna sākṣīkriyāya / na saṃsāre virohati / na nirvāṇam abhinandati / na mokṣaṃ paryeṣate / na bandhaṃ / prakṛtiparinirvṛtā ca sarvadharmān viditvā na saṃsarati na pariṇirvāyati / ayamucyate kāśyapa bhūtapratipattiḥ śramaṇaḥ // bhūtapratipattyā śrāmaṇyāyogaḥ karaṇīya na nāmahetena bhavitavyo ime kāśyapa catvāra śramaṇā / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: KP.125 Now, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who is the <s>śramaṇa</s> of genuine practice? That <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, who has no regard even for body and life — how much less for gain, honor, and reputation. Upon hearing that <s>dharmas</s> are empty, signless, and wishless, he is delighted at heart. Practicing in accordance with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), he is unattached even to <s>nirvāṇa</s> and lives the holy life. How much less would he delight in the three realms? He has no regard even for the view of emptiness — how much less for the view of self, being, life-principle, nourisher, or person. He relies on <s>Dharma</s> and seeks the path of internal liberation from afflictions. He does not run outward. He sees all <s>dharmas</s> as ultimately pure by nature, undefiled. He is an island unto himself, not dependent on another island. He does not perceive the <s>Tathāgata</s> even from the standpoint of <s>Dharma</s> — how much less from the form-body. Even from dispassion, he does not cling to the <s>Dharma</s> — how much less to verbal expression. He does not conceptualize even the unconditioned <s>Dharma</s> as the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> — how much less from the standpoint of a group assembly. He is not devoted to the elimination of any <s>dharma</s>, nor to its cultivation, nor to its direct realization. He does not proliferate in <s>saṃsāra</s>; he does not delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. He does not seek liberation; nor bondage. Having understood all <s>dharmas</s> as primordially quiescent by nature, he neither transmigrates nor attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the <s>śramaṇa</s> of genuine practice. Through genuine practice, the accomplishment of the <s>śramaṇa</s> life should be done, not merely by name. These, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four <s>śramaṇas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
KP.126 yo kāyavākcittamaneraśuddho adāntagupto avinīta lubdho
muṇḍaḥśiraścīvarapātrapāṇī saṃsthānaliṅgā śramaṇeṣu vukto 1
ācāracaryāpsamanvito 'pi rūkṣānnabhojī kuhanādisevī
caturāryavaṃśehi samanvito 'pi saṃsarga durāt parivarjayanto 2
te cāsya sarve na damāya bhonti na śāntaye nāpi ca nirvidāya /
śūnyānimitteṣu prapātasañjñī ācāraguptiḥ kuhako dvitīyoḥ 3
dhutā guṇā śīla śrutaṃ samādhiḥ parasya visvāpanahetu kurvati /

children.text: na śāntaye nāpi ca nirvidāya kīrtīyaślokaśramaṇostṛtīya / 4
children.translated_text: not for peace, not for disenchantment — the third is the <s>śramaṇa</s> of fame and reputation.

children.text: kāyena yo arthika jīvitena vā yo lābhasatkāraparāmukhaśca
children.translated_text: One who has no regard for body, or for life, who has turned away from gain and honor,

children.text: vimokṣa utpādamukhaṃ ca śrutvā anarthikā sarvabhavadgatīṣu / 5 //
children.translated_text: who, upon hearing the gateway of liberation and arising [of wisdom], has no regard for all states of existence —

body.translated_text:
KP.126 One whose body, speech, and mind are impure, untamed, unguarded, untrained, and greedy,
with shaven head, robe, and bowl in hand — among the <s>śramaṇas</s>, this one is called [a <s>śramaṇa</s>] by outer form and marks.
Even one accomplished in conduct and deportment, eating coarse food, practicing deceit and the like,
endowed with the four noble lineages yet avoiding association from afar —
all these [practices] of his are not for taming, not for peace, not for disenchantment;
having the perception of falling into an abyss regarding the empty and signless — the second is the <s>śramaṇa</s> of guarded conduct and deceit.
The <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities), moral conduct, learning, and <s>samādhi</s> — he employs them for inspiring trust in others;

children.text: atyantaśūnyāśca parīkṣa dharmān na nirvṛtiṃ paśyati nāpyanirvṛtiṃ /
children.translated_text: one who examines <s>dharmas</s> as ultimately empty, who sees neither cessation nor non-cessation,

children.text: virāgato dharmamavekṣate sadā asaṃskṛtaṃ dharmam anitya nirvṛtaḥ 6 //
children.translated_text: who always contemplates the <s>Dharma</s> from [the standpoint of] dispassion, who is quiescent regarding the unconditioned <s>Dharma</s> as impermanent —

body.text: KP.127 tadythāpi nāma kāśyapa daridrapuruṣasya samṛdhakośa iti nāmadheyamaṃ bhavet / tatkiṃ manyase kāśyapa anurūpaṃ tasya daridrapuruṣasya tannāmadheyaṃ bhavet / āha no hīdam bhadanta bhagavan / bhagavān āha / evameva kāśyapa ye te śramaṇabrāhmaṇa ityucyante / na ca śramaṇabrāhmaṇasamanvāgatā bhavanti / tān ahaṃ daridiapuruṣān iti vadāmi / tatredamucyate
body.translated_text: KP.127 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a poor man might bear the name 'Rich Treasury' — what do you think, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, would that name be fitting for that poor man? He said: 'No indeed, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, those who are called '<s>śramaṇas</s>' and '<s>brāhmaṇas</s>' yet are not endowed with the qualities of a <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — I call them poor men. Regarding this, it is said:

body.text:
// yathā daridrasya bhaveta nāmaṃ samṛddhakośambhi na tacca śobhate /
śrāmaṇyahīna śramaṇo na śobhate daridra āḍhyetiva ucyamānaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Just as a poor man might bear the name 'Rich Treasury,' but that does not befit him —
a <s>śramaṇa</s> devoid of the <s>śramaṇa</s> life does not befit [the name], like a pauper being called 'wealthy.'

body.text: KP.128 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa kaścideva puruṣo mahatā udakārṇavenohyamānaḥ tṛṣayā kālaṃ kuryāt / evameva kāśyapa ihekatye śramaṇabrāhmaṇo bahun dharmān paryāpnuvanti na rāgatṛṣṇān vinodayanti / na dveṣatṛṣṇā na mohatṛṣṇā śaknuvanti vinodayituṃ / te mahatā dharmārṇavenohyamānā kleśatṛṣāyā kālagatā durgatigāmino bhavanti / tatredamucyate 2 //
body.translated_text: KP.128 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain man, being carried away by a great flood of water, might die of thirst — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, here certain ascetics and brahmins learn many <s>dharmas</s> yet do not dispel the thirst of passion (<s>rāga</s>); they are unable to dispel the thirst of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) or the thirst of delusion (<s>moha</s>). Being carried away by a great flood of <s>Dharma</s>, they die of the thirst of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and become ones destined for unfortunate rebirths (<s>durgati</s>). Herein it is said: 2 //

children.text: yathā manuṣyo udakārṇavena uhyanti tṛṣṇāya kareya kālam /
children.translated_text: Just as a person carried by the flood of water would die of thirst,

children.text: tathā paṭhantā bahudharmatṛṣṇayā dharmārṇavasthāmi vrajantyapāyaṃ //
children.translated_text: so too those who recite [texts] — by the thirst for many <s>dharmas</s>, standing in the flood of <s>Dharma</s>, they go to unfortunate rebirths. //

body.text: KP.129 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa vaidyo oṣadhabhāraṃ gṛhītvā anuvicaret tasya kaścid eva vyādhi utpadyeta na ca taṃ vyādhi śaknuyācikitsituṃ / evameva kāśyapa bahuśrutasya kleśavyādhi draṣṭavyā yastena śrutena na śaknoti ātmanaḥ kleṣavyādhi cikitsituṃ / nirarthakaṃ tasya tacchrutaṃ bhaviṣyati / tatredamucyate 3 //
body.translated_text: KP.129 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a physician, having taken up a load of medicines, might wander about, and then some disease might arise in him, yet he would be unable to cure that disease — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, one should view the affliction-disease of the learned one who, with that learning, is unable to cure his own affliction-disease. That learning of his will be useless. Herein it is said: 3 //

children.text: yatheva vaidyauṣadharbharastrasaṃsthe parilhrameta nikhilaṃhi loke /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician, burdened with medicines, might wander everywhere through the world,

children.text: utpannavyādhīn a nivartayeca nirarthakaṃ tasya bhaveta taṃ hi /
children.translated_text: yet if diseases arise, he cannot avert them — that [medicine] would be useless for him;

children.text: bhikṣustathā śīlaguṇerupetaḥ śrutena yukto 'pi na ca ścikitset /
children.translated_text: so too a monk endowed with the qualities of moral conduct, though joined with learning, does not heal [himself];

children.text: ayoniśa kleśasamutthitā rujā vṛthā śramastasya śrutābhiyogaḥ //
children.translated_text: the illness born of afflictions due to wrong attention — his exertion in learning is in vain. //

body.text: KP.130 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa / glānaḥ puruṣo rājārhan bhaiṣajyam upayujyāsaṃvareṇa kālaṃ kuryāt / evameva kāśyapa bahuśrutasya kleśavyādhiṃ draṣṭavyāḥ yastenāsṃvareṇa kālaṃ karoti / yo rājārhāṃ bhaiṣajyāṃ paryāpunitvā asaṃvareṇa apāyagāmī bhavati / tatredamucyate 4 //
body.translated_text: KP.130 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a sick person worthy of royal treatment, having taken medicine, might die through lack of restraint — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, one should view the affliction-disease of the learned one who, through lack of restraint, meets his end — who, having obtained medicine worthy of a king, becomes one destined for unfortunate rebirths through lack of restraint. Herein it is said: 4 //

body.text:
yathāpi rājārhaṃ pītva bheṣajaṃ vrajennaro saṃvarato nipātaṃ /
bahuśrutasyeṣa tu kleśavyādhir yo saṃvareṇeha karoti kālam /
body.translated_text: Just as having drunk a medicine worthy of a king, a man might fall from [lack of] restraint — so is the affliction-disease of the learned one who, through [lack of] restraint here, meets his end.

body.text: KP.131 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa anarghaṃ vaiḍūryamahāmaṇiratnam uccāre patitam akāryopakaṃ bhavati / evameva kāśyapa bahuśrutasya lābhasatkārauccārapatanaṃ draṣṭavya / niṣkiñcanaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu / tatredamucyate 5 //
body.translated_text: KP.131 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a priceless great <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem, having fallen into excrement, becomes of no use — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, one should view the fall of the learned one through gain and honor into excrement — [becoming] without anything of value among gods and humans. Herein it is said: 5 //

body.text:
ratnaṃ yathoccāragataṃ juguspitaṃ yathā syānna tathā yathā pura /
bahuśrutasyāpi vadāmi bhikṣoḥ satkāramīḍe patanaṃ tatheva /
body.translated_text: Just as a gem fallen into excrement is disgusting and is not as it was before — even so, I say, for the learned monk too, the fall through honor and gain is likewise.

body.text: // tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapā tadeva vaiḍūryaṃ mahāmaṇiratnam ameddhyāvaskarāduddhṛtaṃ bhavet suddhautaṃ suprakṣālitaṃ suparimārjitaṃ / taṃ maṇiratnasvabhāvam eva na vijahatyevameva kāśyapa bahuśruto 'lpaprayatnena sarvakleśān viśodhayati mahāprajñāratnasvabhāvam eva na vijahāti 6 / //
body.translated_text: // Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that very same great <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem, when retrieved from the impure refuse heap, washed well, rinsed well, and polished well — it does not abandon its inherent gem-nature — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the learned one, with little effort, purifies all afflictions and does not abandon his inherent nature as a gem of great wisdom. 6 //

body.text: KP.132 tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa mṛtakasya śirasi suvarṇamālā / evameva kāśyapa duḥśīlasya kāṣāyadhāraṇaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ / tatredamucyate / 7 //
body.translated_text: KP.132 Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a gold garland on the head of a corpse — even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, one should view the wearing of the saffron robe by one of bad moral conduct. Herein it is said: 7 //

kāṣāyavastrāṇi tathā viśīle dṛṣṭvā 'nna kuryān manasaḥ pradoṣāṃ //
body.translated_text: Just as a gold garland or a flower garland placed on the head of a corpse — so too one should view saffron robes on one of bad conduct; having seen this, one should not generate ill-will in the mind. //

body.translated_text: KP.134 There are, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, four who are immoral yet counterfeit the virtuous. What are the four? Here, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a certain [...] monk dwells restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of discipline); endowed with proper conduct and range of activity; seeing danger in the slightest faults; properly [...] training in the training rules; endowed with purified bodily, verbal, and mental actions; of purified livelihood — yet he [...] holds the view of self. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, should be viewed as the first who is immoral yet counterfeits the virtuous. // Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, here a certain monk is a master of the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic discipline); established in the performance of the <s>Vinaya</s> and the guarding of the <s>Vinaya</s> — yet the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) remains unshaken in him. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the second who is immoral yet counterfeits the virtuous. // Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, here a certain monk dwells in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), endowed with [...] compassion toward beings — yet when he hears of the unborn nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, he is frightened, terrified, and falls into terror. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the third who is immoral yet counterfeits the virtuous. // Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, here a certain monk possesses the twelve <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities) [...] yet holds the view of apprehension and is established in the notion of 'I.' This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the fourth who is immoral yet counterfeits the virtuous. These [...], <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are the four who are immoral yet counterfeit the virtuous. //

body.text: KP.135 śīlam śīlam iti kāśyapa ucyate / yatra nātma..................... nātmīya na sattvo na sattvaprajñaptiḥ na kriyā nākriyā / na karaṇaṃ nākaraṇaṃ / cāro nācāraḥ na pracā................. nāpracāraḥ na nāmaṃ na rūpa / nimittaṃ nānimittaṃ / na śamo napraśamaḥ na grāho notsargaḥ na grāhyaṃ ............... hya / na sattvo na sattvaprajñaptiḥ na vāṅ na vākprajñapti na cittaṃ na cittaprajñaptiḥ na loko nālokaḥ na niśrayo nāniśrayaḥ nā maśīlotkarṣaṇā / na paraduḥśīlapaṃsanā / na śīlamanyanā / na śīlakalpanā / vikalpanā / na saṅkalpanā na parikalpanā / iyamucyate kāśyapa āryāṇā śīla / anāsravam aparyāpannaṃ traidhātukānu gataṃ sarvaniśrayāpagaṃ /
body.translated_text: KP.135 'Moral conduct, moral conduct' — thus, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, it is said. Where there is no self [...], no mine, no being, no designation of a being; no action and no non-action; no doing and no not-doing; no sphere and no non-sphere; no conduct [...] and no non-conduct; no name and no form; no sign and no signlessness; no tranquility and no non-tranquility; no grasping and no letting go; no graspable and no [...]; no being and no designation of a being; no speech and no designation of speech; no mind and no designation of mind; no world and no non-world; no support and no non-support; no exalting one's own morality; no denigrating others' immorality; no conceit regarding morality; no conceptualizing morality — no discrimination, no intention, no false conceptualization. This, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the morality of the noble ones (<s>ārya</s>) — without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), not included [in the three realms], not conforming to the three realms, free from all supports.

children.translated_text: Not stained by the world, not relying on the world; having attained the light, without possessiveness [...], without anything; not perceiving self, not perceiving others — having fully understood perception, one is of purified morality. 4. One for whom there is no far shore, no near shore, no middle, [...] never attached to the far shore and beyond, unbound, unattached, without deceit, without outflows —

children.text: sa śīlavān kāśyapa buddhaśāsane / 5
children.translated_text: that one is virtuous, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching. 5

body.translated_text: The virtuous one has nothing whatsoever [...]; the virtuous one has no intoxication and no support; the virtuous one has no darkness and no bondage; the virtuous one has no passion and no [...]. Peaceful, calmed, with a tranquil mind, free from conceptualization and discrimination, without defilement, liberated from all conceit and pride [...] — [that is] morality, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching. Not regarding the body, not seeking after one's life, desireless regarding all existences and rebirths, rightly gone [...] established,

children.translated_text: for whom there is no self here nor anything belonging to a self — to that extent one is declared established in morality. 6
