na śikṣayā manyati prātimokṣe na cāpi tena bhavateha tanmayo /
athottaraṃ margati āryamārge viśuddhaśīlasya ime nimittā 7
na śīlaparamo na samādhitannmayoḥ paryeṣate duttari prajñābhāvanā /
anopalambham āryāṇa gotraṃ viśuddhaśīla sugataṃ praśastam /
satkāyadṛṣṭe hi vimuktamānaso ahaṃ mamaitīha na tasya bhoti /
children.translated_text: One does not take pride in training through the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, nor does one become identified with it. But one seeks further on the noble path — these are the signs of one whose morality is purified. 7. One is not fixated on morality alone nor absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> alone; one seeks the supreme cultivation of wisdom beyond. Non-apprehension is the lineage of the noble ones — purified morality, praised by the <s>Sugata</s>. With a mind freed from the view of the existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), 'I' and 'mine' do not exist here for such a one.

children.text: adhimucyate śūnyatabuddhagocaramm imasya śīlasya samo na vidyate / 9
children.translated_text: One is convinced of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> — the equal of this morality is not to be found. 9

children.text: śīle pratiṣṭhāya samādhi śuddhaḥ samādhiprāptasya ca prajñabhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Established in morality, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is purified; and for one who has attained <s>samādhi</s>, there is the cultivation of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).

children.text: prajñāya jñānaṃ bhavate viśuddhaṃ viśuddhajñānasya ca śīlasampadā / 10 //
children.translated_text: Through wisdom, purified knowledge arises; and for one of purified knowledge, there is the perfection of morality. 10 //

body.translated_text: KP.137 With a mind unattached to name and form, concentrated, with a well-tamed mind,

body.text: KP.138 asmin khalu punargāthābhinirhāre bhāṣyamāṇe aṣṭānāṃ bhikṣuśatānām anupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni / dvātriṃśatināṃ ca prāṇasahasrāṇāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddhaṃ / pañca bhikṣuśatāni dhyānalābhī uthāyāsanebhyaḥ prakrāntāni imāṃ gambhīrā dharmadeśanām avataranto nāvagāhamānāḥ anadhimucyamānāḥ
body.translated_text: KP.138 When this verse-exposition was being spoken, the minds of eight hundred monks were liberated from the outflows without clinging. And for thirty-two thousand beings, the pure, stainless, dust-free <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (dharma-eye) was purified regarding dharmas. Five hundred monks who were <s>dhyāna</s>-attainers rose from their seats and departed, not penetrating, not plunging into, not having faith in this profound dharma-teaching.

body.text: KP.139 athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapo bhagavantam etadavocat imāni bhagavan pañca bhikṣuṣatāni dhyānalābhīnyutthāyāsanebhyaḥ prakrāntāni / imām gambhīrā dharmadeśanām avataranto nāvagāhanto manadhimucyamānāḥ bhagavān āha / tathā hyete kāśyapa bhikṣuvaḥ anadhimānite manadhimucyamānā imāṃ gambhīrā gāthābhinirhārām anāsravaṃ śīlaviśuddhinirdeśaṃ śrutvā nāvataranti nādhimucyanti nāvagāhanti tatkasmāddheto gambhīro yaṃ kāśyapa gāthābhinirhāraṃ gambhīraṃ buddhā bhagavantānāṃ bodhi sā na śakyam anavaropitakuśalamūle pāpamatraparigṛhīteranadhimuktibahule sattvairadhimucyituṃ vā paryapanituṃ vā avatarituṃ vā /
body.translated_text: KP.139 Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, these five hundred monks who are <s>dhyāna</s>-attainers have risen from their seats and departed, not penetrating, not plunging into, not having faith in this profound dharma-teaching." The Blessed One said: "Indeed so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, these monks, lacking confidence, having no faith, upon hearing this profound verse-exposition, this instruction on the purification of outflow-free moral conduct, do not penetrate it, do not have faith in it, do not plunge into it. And why? Because this verse-exposition is profound, <s>Kāśyapa</s>; the awakening of the Blessed Buddhas is profound. It cannot be penetrated, comprehended, or entered into by beings in whom wholesome roots have not been planted, who are seized by evil <s>Māra</s>, and in whom lack of faith is abundant."

body.text: KP.140 api ca kāśyapa etāni pañca bhikṣuśatāni kāśyapasya tathāgatasyārhata samyaksambuddhasya pravacane anyatīrthikaśrāvakā abhūvan / ste kāśyapasya tathāgatasyāntikāduparambhābhiprāyairekā dharmadeśanā śrutvā śrutvā ceva cittaprasādo labdha āścāryaṃ yāvanmadhurapriyabhākhalveyaṃ kāśyapastathāgato 'rhāṃ saṃyaksambuddha iti / te tataścyutasamānā ekacittaprasādena kālagatāḥ trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannāḥ neva hetunā iha mamma śāsane pravrajitāḥ tānyetāni kāśyapa pañca bhikṣuśatāni dṛṣṭigatapraskanditāni imāṃ gambhīrā dharmadeśanā nāvataranti nāvagāhanti nādhimucyante na śraddadhanti / kṛtaṃ punareṣā m.... yaṃ dharmadeśanāyā parikarma na bhūyo vinipātagāmino bhaviṣyanti / ebhireva skandhaiḥ parinirvāsyanti / //
body.translated_text: KP.140 "Moreover, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, these five hundred monks were, under the dispensation of the <s>Tathāgata Kāśyapa</s>, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Awakened One, followers of other sects. They, having heard a single dharma-teaching from the <s>Tathāgata Kāśyapa</s> with the intention of finding fault, nevertheless gained mental clarity: 'How wonderful! How sweet and pleasing is the speech of the <s>Tathāgata Kāśyapa</s>, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Awakened One!' Having died and departed from there through that single moment of mental clarity, they were reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. It is precisely by that cause that they have gone forth in my dispensation here. These five hundred monks, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, have stumbled into wrong views and do not penetrate, do not plunge into, do not have faith in, do not believe this profound dharma-teaching. Yet this [...] serves as a preparation for the dharma-teaching; they will no longer be destined for downfall. They will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> within these very aggregates."

body.text: KP.141 tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim āmantrayati sma / gacchastvaṃsubhūte etān bhikṣu sañjñapaya subhūtirāha / bhagavata eva tāvadete bhikṣavo bhāṣitaṃ prativilomayanti kaḥ punarvādo mama / atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyā yena mārgeṇa te bhikṣavo gacchanti sma / tasminmārge dvau bhikṣu nirmimīte sma / atha tāni pañca bhikṣuśatāni yena mārgeṇa tau dvau bhikṣu nirmito tenopasaṅkrāmannupasaṅkramyevamavocan / kutra āyuṣmanto gamiṣyathaḥ tāvavocatāḥ gamiṣyāma vayam araṇyāyataneṣu sukhaṃ phāṣaṃ vihariṣyāmaḥ tatkasmāddhetoryaṃ hi bhagavān dharmaṃ deśayati tāmāvā dharmadeśanāṃ nāvarāvo nāvagāhāma he / nadhimucyāvahe / utrasivaḥ santrasāvaḥ santrāsamāpadyāmahe / tāvāvām āraṇyāyataneṣu sukhaṃ vihariṣyāmaḥ
body.translated_text: KP.141 Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: "Go, <s>Subhūti</s>, and bring those monks to understanding." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Even the words spoken by the Blessed One himself these monks reject — how much more so mine!" Then at that moment the Blessed One magically emanated two monks on the path by which those monks were going. Then those five hundred monks approached the two emanated monks on the path and, having approached, said: "Where are you venerable ones going?" Those two said: "We shall go to the forest hermitages; we shall dwell in comfort and ease. And why? Because we do not penetrate the dharma that the Blessed One teaches; we do not plunge into that dharma-teaching. We have no faith in it. We are frightened, terrified, and overcome with terror. So we two shall dwell in comfort in the forest hermitages."

body.text: KP.142 tānyapi pañca bhikṣuśatānyetad avocan / vayam apyāyuṣmanto bhagavato dharmadeśanā nāvatarāmo nāvagāhāmahe nādhimucyāmahe / utrasāvaḥ santrasāvaḥ santrāsam āpadyāmahe / te vayam araṇyāyaneṣu dhyānasukhavihārairvihariṣyāmaḥ nirmitakāvavocatā saṅgāyiṣyāma vayam āyuṣmanto na vivadiṣyāmaḥ avivāda paramo hi śramaṇadharmaḥ yadiha māyuṣmanta ityucyate parinirvāṇam iti / katamaḥ sa dharmo yaḥ pari .............. syati kaścit punarasmiṃ kaye ātmā vā sattvo vā jīvo vā janturvā pauṣau vā pudgalo vā manujo vā mānavo................... kartā vā kārako vā vedako vā jānako vā sañjānako vā utthāpako vā samutthāpako vā yaḥ parinirvāsyati /
body.translated_text: KP.142 Those five hundred monks also said: "We too, venerable ones, do not penetrate the Blessed One's dharma-teaching, do not plunge into it, do not have faith in it. We are frightened, terrified, and overcome with terror. So we shall dwell in forest hermitages, abiding in the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s>." The emanated ones said: "Let us confer together, venerable ones; we shall not dispute. For freedom from dispute is the highest quality of an ascetic. If, venerable ones, it is said that there is '<s>parinirvāṇa</s>' — what is that dharma which attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> [...]? Is there in this body a self, or a being, or a soul, or a creature, or a person, or an individual, or a human, or a mortal, [...] or a doer, or an agent, or a feeler, or a knower, or a perceiver, or an instigator, or an initiator, who will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?"

body.text: KP.143 te āhu................... na kvacidasti / asmiṃ kāye ātmā vā sattvo vā jīvo vā janturvā puruṣo vā pudgalo vā manujo vā mānavo vā kartā vā kārako vā vedako vā jānako vā sañjānako vā utthāpako vā yaḥ parinirvāsyati / nirmitakā prāhu / X puna sākṣīkṛyāyā parinirvāsyatīti / te āhuḥ rāgakṣayāya dveṣakṣayāya mohakṣayāya āyuṣmanta parinirvāṇam iti / nirmitakā prāhuḥ kiṃ punarāyuṣmatā rāgadveṣamohāḥ saṃvidyante yāṃ kṣapayiṣyatha / te āhu / na te ādhyātmena na bahirdhā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyante / nāpi te aparikalpitā utpadyante nirmitakāv avocatā / tena māyuṣmanto māsmān kalpayataḥ māsman vikalpayataḥ yadāyuṣmanto na kalpayiṣyathaḥ na vikalpayiṣyathaḥ tadāyuṣmanto na raṅkṣyatha na viraṅkṣyathaḥ yaścāyuṣmanto na rakto na viraktaḥ................... śānta ityucyate /
body.translated_text: KP.143 They said: "[...] There is nowhere in this body a self, or a being, or a soul, or a creature, or a person, or an individual, or a human, or a mortal, or a doer, or an agent, or a feeler, or a knower, or a perceiver, or an instigator who will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>." The emanated ones said: "[...] what then is directly realized when one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?" They said: "<s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, venerable ones, is for the destruction of passion, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion." The emanated ones said: "But do passion, hatred, and delusion exist in you venerable ones, that you would destroy them?" They said: "They are not found internally, nor externally, nor in between. Nor do they arise without being conceptually constructed." The emanated ones said: "Therefore, venerable ones, do not construct concepts about us, do not discriminate about us. When, venerable ones, you will not construct and will not discriminate, then, venerable ones, you will neither be attached nor detached. And one who, venerable ones, is neither attached nor detached [...] is called 'at peace.'"

body.text: KP.144 śīlam āyuṣmanto na saṃsarati na parinirvāti samādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanam āyuṣ................. na saṃsarati na parinirvāti / ebhiścevāyuṣmanto dharmai nirvāṇaṃ sūcyate / ete ca dharmā śūnyā viviktā agrā...................... prajahīte tāmāyuṣmantaḥ sañjñā yaduta parinirvāṇam iti mā ca sañjñāyā sañjñā kārṣvaḥ mā asañjñāyā.................... ca sañjñayā sañjñā parijñāsiṣva / yaḥ sañjñayā sañjñā parijānāti sañjñābandhanam evāsya tad bhavati / saṃ................ vedayitanirodhasamā pattimāyuṣmantaḥ samāpadyadhvaṃ mā ca kalpayatha mā vikalpayathaḥ sañjñāvedayita................... dhasamāpattisamāpannasya bhikṣornāstyuttare karaṇīyam iti vadāmaḥ
body.translated_text: KP.144 "Moral conduct, venerable ones, neither transmigrates nor attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation, venerable ones, [...] neither transmigrate nor attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And by these very dharmas, venerable ones, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is indicated. And these dharmas are empty, isolated, supreme [...]. Abandon, venerable ones, that notion — namely '<s>parinirvāṇa</s>' — and do not construct a notion from that notion, nor [...] fully comprehend that notion through the notion itself. For whoever fully comprehends a notion through a notion, for him that becomes merely a bondage of notions. [...] Venerable ones, enter the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, but do not construct and do not discriminate. [...] Of a monk who has entered the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, we do not say that there is anything further to be done."

body.text: KP.145 asmiṃ khalu punardharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe........................... ṣāṃ pañcānāṃ bhikṣuśatānām anupādāyāsravebhyaḥ cittāni vimuktāni / te vimuktacittā yena bhagavāṃste................... pasaṅkramannupasaṅkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā ekānte myaṣīdan / athāyuṣmān subhutistā....................... kṣu etad avocat / kva nu khalvāyuṣmanto gatā kuto vā āgatāḥ te avocanakvacidgamanāya / na kutaścidāga........................... nāya / bhadanta subhūte bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ subhūtirāha / ko nāmāyuṣmantā śāstā / te āhuḥ yotpanno................. rinirvāsyati /
body.translated_text: KP.145 When this dharma-discourse was being spoken, [...] the minds of the five hundred monks were liberated from the outflows without clinging. Those monks, their minds liberated, went to where the Blessed One was; [...] having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down on one side. Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> [...] said this to those monks: "Where indeed, venerable ones, did you go, and whence have you come?" They said: "There was no going anywhere, nor coming from anywhere. [...] Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the dharma has been taught by the Blessed One." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Who, venerable ones, is your teacher?" They said: "He who has arisen [...] will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."

body.text: KP.146 subhūtirāha / kasya yuṣme śrāvakā kasya sakāśādyuṣme vinītā te āhuryena na prāptanābhisaṃ................... subhūtirāha / kasya sakāśādyuṣmākaṃ dharmaṃ śrutaṃ / te āhu yasya na skandhā na dhātavo nāyatanāni 3 subhūtirāha / kathaṃ punaryuṣme dharmaṃ śrutaṃ / te āhurna bandhanāya na mokṣāya / 4 subhūtirāha / kathaṃ yūyaṃ pra................... ktā te āhu / na yogāya na prayogāya / na prahāṇāya / 5 subhūtirāha kena yūyaṃ vinītāḥ te āhuḥ yasya na kāyapāriniṣpattirna cittapracāraṃ / 6 subhūtirāha / kathaṃ yuṣmābhi prayujyamānā vimuktāḥ.................. āhuḥ nāvidyaprabāṇāya na vidyotpādāya 7
body.translated_text: KP.146 <s>Subhūti</s> said: "Whose disciples are you? By whom were you trained?" They said: "By one who has not attained nor realized [...]." <s>Subhūti</s> said: "From whom did you hear the dharma?" They said: "From one who has no aggregates, no elements, no sense-bases." (3) <s>Subhūti</s> said: "How then did you hear the dharma?" They said: "Not for bondage, not for liberation." (4) <s>Subhūti</s> said: "How were you [...] instructed?" They said: "Not for practice, not for exertion, not for abandonment." (5) <s>Subhūti</s> said: "By whom were you trained?" They said: "By one who has no perfection of body, no activity of mind." (6) <s>Subhūti</s> said: "How, having applied yourselves, were you liberated?" [...] They said: "Not for the destruction of ignorance, not for the arising of knowledge." (7)

body.text: KP.147 subhūtirāha / kasya yūyaṃ śrāvakāḥ te āhuḥ yasya na prāpto nā.................... sambuddhaḥ 8 subhūtirāha / keva cirena yūyaṃ parinirvāsyathaḥ tāhuḥ yāvaccireṇa tathāgatanirmi.................... kāḥ parinirvāsyanti tā vaccireṇa vayaṃ parinirvāsyāmaḥ 9 subhūtirāha / kṛtaṃ yuṣmābhi svakārtha........................... te āhuḥ arthānupalabdhatvāt 10 subhūtirāha / kṛtaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīya / te āhu / kārakānupa...................... bdhitvāt / subhūtirāha / keva yuṣmākaṃ sabrahmacāriṇa / te āhuḥ / ye traidhātuke nopa caranti / na pracaraṃ.................
body.translated_text: KP.147 <s>Subhūti</s> said: Whose <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) are you? They replied: Of him who has not attained [...] the Perfectly Awakened One. 8. <s>Subhūti</s> said: How long will it be before you attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? They replied: As long as the emanations created by the <s>Tathāgata</s> [...] will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, so long will we attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. 9. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Have you accomplished your own purpose? [...] They replied: Because purpose is unapprehensible. 10. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Have you completed what needed to be done? They replied: Because the doer is [...] unapprehensible. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Who are your companions in the holy life? They replied: Those who do not wander or course in the three realms [...].

body.text: KP.148 subhūtirāha / kṣīṇā yūṣmākaṃ kleśāḥ te āhuratyantakṣayatvāt sarvadharmāṇāṃ 13 subhūtirāha / dharṣitā yu...................... r māraḥ te āhuḥ skandhamārānupalabdhitvāt 14 / subhūtirāha / paricīrṇo yuṣmābhistathāgataḥ te āhuḥ..................... kāyena na cittena 15 subhūtirāha / sthitā yuṣmākaṃ dākṣīṇeyabhūmauḥ te āhuḥ agrāhataḥ a........................... tigrāhataḥ 16 subhūtirāha / cchinnā yūyaṃ saṃsāraṃ / te āhuḥ anuccheda aśāśvatatvāt 17 subhūtirāha / pratipannā yūyaṃ śramaṇaśramaṇabhūmau / tena punarāhuḥ asaṅgāvimuktau / 18 subhūtirā........................ kigāmināyuṣmantaḥ te āhuḥryadgaminastathāgatanirmitāḥ 19 //
body.translated_text: KP.148 <s>Subhūti</s> said: Are your <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) exhausted? They replied: Because of the absolute exhaustion of all <s>dharmas</s>. 13. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Have you [...] vanquished <s>Māra</s>? They replied: Because <s>skandha-māra</s> (the Māra of the aggregates) is unapprehensible. 14. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Have you served the <s>Tathāgata</s>? They replied: [...] not by body, not by mind. 15. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Are you established on the ground worthy of offerings? They replied: Through non-grasping [...] and through non-excessive-grasping. 16. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Have you cut off <s>saṃsāra</s>? They replied: Because it is neither annihilated nor eternal. 17. <s>Subhūti</s> said: Have you entered the ground of the <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant)? They again replied: Through non-attachment and liberation. 18. <s>Subhūti</s> [...] said: Where are you going, venerable ones? They replied: Wherever the emanations of the <s>Tathāgata</s> go. 19.

body.text: KP.149 iti hyāyuṣmantaḥ subhūti paripṛcchataḥ teṣā......................... bhikṣūṇāṃ visarjayantānāṃ / tasyā parṣadi aṣṭānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāṃ pañcānāṃ ca bhikṣuṇīśatānām anupādāya................. vebhyaścittāni vimuktāni / dvātriṃśatīnāṃ ca prāṇasahasrāṇāṃ sadevamānuṣikāyāṃ prajāyām virajo vigata ..................... dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham //
body.translated_text: KP.149 Thus, as the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> was questioning and those [...] monks were answering, in that assembly, the minds of eight hundred monks and five hundred nuns were liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (taints) without grasping. And for thirty-two thousand beings, including gods and humans, the pure and stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye [...] regarding <s>dharmas</s> was purified.

body.text: KP.150 atha khalu samantāloko nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametad avocat i......................... gavan mahāratnakūṭe dharmaparyāye śikṣitukāmena bodhisattvena kathaṃ sthātavyaṃ kathaṃ pratipattavyaṃ / kathaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ ....................... vānāha / udgṛhya kulaputra iha dharmaparyāye śikṣā ākhyātā pratipattisārāṇāṃ satpuruṣāṇām iyaṃ dharmaparyāyo bhavārthakaro bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: KP.150 Then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Samantāloka</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: [...] <s>Bhagavān</s>, for one who wishes to train in this <s>Mahāratnakūṭa</s> (Great Jewel-Heap) <s>Dharma</s> discourse, how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> stand, how should he practice, how should he train? [...] The Blessed One said: Having taken up this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, O son of good family, the training has been declared for those noble beings whose essence is practice. This <s>Dharma</s> discourse will be productive of benefit in existence.

body.text: KP.151 tadyathāpi nāma kulaputra kaścideva puruṣaḥ mṛnmayīnāvabhiruhyaṃ gaṅgānadīm uttartukāmo bhavet / tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra kīdṛśena vīryeṇa tena puruṣeṇa sā nnorvāhayitavyā bhave................... ha balavatā bhagavan vīryeṇa / tatkasmāddhetoḥ mā measamprāptapārasyevāntareṇa nnaurvipadyeta / mahāo....................... rṇavaprāpto smin mā haivāntareṇāyaṃ nāvā vikīryeta / bhagavān āha / evameva samantāloka ato bahutare..................... balavantatareṇa vīryeṇa bodhisattvena bodhiḥ samudānayitavyāḥ mahābalavīryeṇa ca buddhadharmā samudānayita........................
body.translated_text: KP.151 It is as if, O son of good family, some man were to board a boat made of clay, wishing to cross the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. What do you think, O son of good family — with what kind of effort should that man propel that boat? [...] He replied: With mighty effort, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Why? Lest the boat break apart midway before reaching the other shore. [And] having reached the great [...] ocean, lest the boat disintegrate midway. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Just so, <s>Samantāloka</s>, with even greater and mightier effort must the <s>bodhisattva</s> bring awakening to accomplishment, and with great strength and effort must the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities be brought to accomplishment [...].

body.text: KP.152 evamanasīkāreṇa anityo batāyaṃ kāyaḥ caturmahābhūtikaḥ mātāpitṛkalalasambhūta / adhru....................... nāśvāsikaḥ vipariṇāmadharmaḥ ucchadasnapanaparimardanabhedanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmaḥ oda .......................... lmāsopacitaḥ acirasthāyi anāhāro na tiṣṭhati / jarjaragṛhasadṛśo durabalaḥ mā haiva anādattasā....................... syāntareṇa kālakriyā bhaviṣyati mahoghārṇavaprāpto 'smi caturottararogaśataprāptānāṃ sattvānām uhyamāna ......................... m uttāraṇatāyā bodhisattvena mahādharmanāvaṃ samudānayiṣyāmi / yayā dharmanāvā sarvasattvā saṃsār......................... vaprāptān uhyamānān uttārayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: KP.152 With such mental attention [one should reflect]: 'Alas, this body is impermanent, composed of the four great elements, born from the union of mother and father, unreliable [...], subject to change, subject to destruction through breaking, washing, rubbing, splitting, scattering, and disintegrating [...], built up from [...] impurities, not long-lasting, unable to subsist without nourishment, like a dilapidated house, without strength. Lest, before having obtained [what must be obtained] [...], death should occur midway — I have reached the great flood-ocean. For the sake of ferrying across beings who are afflicted by four hundred and more diseases, who are being carried away [...], I, as a <s>bodhisattva</s>, shall bring to accomplishment the great <s>Dharma</s>-boat, by which <s>Dharma</s>-boat I shall ferry across all beings who are being carried away in the [...] ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

body.text:
KP.153 tatra samantāloka kīdṛśe dharmanau bodhisatvasya samudānayi....................... iha samantāloka bodhisattvena dharmanāvā samudānayitavyā yaduta sarvasamacittasambhārā.................... vanti anantapuṇyopacitā śīlaphalanirjātā dānaparivārālaṅkārālaṅkṛtāḥ āśayadṛḍhasārab........................ nasubaddhāḥ kṣāntisoratyasmṛtiśalyabaddhāḥ saptabodhyaṅgasambhāradṛḍhavīryakuśaladharmadārusamudānitā dhyān.................... ttakramanīyakarmaṇikṛtāḥ dāntāśāntājāneyakuśalaśilpasuniṣṭhitā / atyantākopyadharma mahākaruṇāsaṅgṛhī........................ catuḥsaṅgrahavastuśūraturagavāhinī pratyarthikaprajñājñānasupratirakṣitā /
upāyakauśalyasukṛtavic.................... catubrahmavihārasuśodhitāṃ /
body.translated_text: KP.153 Now, <s>Samantāloka</s>, what kind of <s>Dharma</s>-boat should the <s>bodhisattva</s> bring to accomplishment [...]? Here, <s>Samantāloka</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should bring to accomplishment the <s>Dharma</s>-boat — namely, one equipped with the provisions of equanimity toward all, [...] accumulated with boundless merit, produced from the fruit of moral conduct, adorned with the ornament of the retinue of generosity, firmly bound with the rope of firm resolve, [...] fastened with the bolts of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), forbearance, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and vigilance, constructed from the timber of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), firm effort, and wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, [...] made navigable through the workmanship of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), completed with the fine craftsmanship of the tamed, the peaceful, and the noble, of indestructible <s>dharma</s>, held together by great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), [...] driven by the heroic horses of the four means of attraction (<s>saṅgrahavastu</s>), well-guarded by the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) against adversaries, [...] well-constructed through skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), well-purified through the four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes).

body.text: KP.154 catusmṛtyupasthānasucintitakāyopanītā / samyakprahāṇaprasaṭhāri ................ dajavajavitā / indriyasunirīkṣitadānavakravigata balavegasamudgatā antareṇa śithilabodhyaṅgavibodha..................... ariśatrumārapathajahanī mānokramavāhinī / kutirthyatīrthajahanī / śamathaniddhyaptinirdiṣṭā vipaśyanāpra ................ gā / ubhayorantayorasaktavāhinī / hetudharmayuktā vipulvistīrṇākṣayaprahāṇābandhā vighuṣṭaśabdā daśa................... kṣu śabdam ādāyatyāgacchatāgacchatābhiruta mahādharmanāvaṃ nirvāṇapuragāminī / kṣemamārgagāminī / mahā.................. matīra satkāyadṛṣṭiṃ jahanīṃ / parimatīragāminī laghusarvadṛṣṭigatavigatāṃ /
body.translated_text: KP.154 Its hull is well-fashioned through the well-contemplated four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>). Its [...] oars are swift through the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>). Its speed is surpassing through the well-observed faculties (<s>indriya</s>), free from deficiency in generosity and morality, generated with the momentum of the powers (<s>bala</s>), [...] awakening through the factors of awakening [...], abandoning the path of the enemy <s>Māra</s>, navigating away from arrogance, abandoning the fords of false teachers, directed toward <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and contemplation, propelled by <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), [...] navigating unattached to both extremes, endowed with the <s>Dharma</s> of causes, vast, extensive, inexhaustible, [...] of resounding sound, sending forth its call in the ten [...] directions: 'Come, come!' — the great <s>Dharma</s>-boat heading toward the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, traveling the safe path, [...] the great shore, abandoning the view of the self-aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), reaching the further shore, light and free from all views.

body.translated_text: KP.155 Such, O son of good family, is the <s>Dharma</s> [...] that the <s>bodhisattva</s> should bring to accomplishment, with a mind wearied over immeasurable <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (eons). [...] For the welfare of all beings, by this true <s>Dharma</s>-boat all beings who are being carried away in the four floods should be ferried across. Such [...] a boat, O son of good family, should the <s>bodhisattva</s> bring to accomplishment. Now, <s>Samantāloka</s>, what is the swift higher knowledge (<s>kṣiprābhijñatā</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s>? Namely, effortless [...] exertion toward all beings; intense zeal through the purity of aspiration; blazing energy in the accumulation of all roots of merit; [...] zeal for the wholesome through wise attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>); contentment with learning through the fulfillment of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); humility through [...] reliance on wisdom; going forth into homelessness; dwelling in the forest for the fulfillment of all virtues, through the seclusion of body and mind.

body.text: KP.156 asaṃsargo durja........................... navivarjanatayā / dharmārthikatā paramārthārthapratisaraṇatayā / jñānārtho tyantakopanārthatayā / dharmā..................... nārthatayā / satyārtho avisaṃvādanārthatayā / śunyatārtho samyakprayogārthatayā / vivekārtho atyantopa.................. rthatāyeti // iyamucyate samantāloka bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya kṣiprābhijñatā //
body.translated_text: KP.156 Non-association, through the avoidance of [...] bad company; seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, through reliance on the ultimate meaning (<s>paramārtha</s>); the purpose of knowledge, through the purpose of [...] absolute [...]; the purpose of the <s>Dharma</s>, through [...]; the purpose of truth, through the purpose of non-deception; the purpose of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), through the purpose of right practice; the purpose of seclusion, through the purpose of absolute [...] tranquility. This, <s>Samantāloka</s>, is called the swift higher knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

aścāryaṃ sugataḥ yāvacceyaṃ mahāratnakūṭo sūtrāntarā ......................... upakārībhūto mahāyānasamprasthitānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ ca kuladuhitṛṇāṃ ca / kiyadbhagavan sa kulaputro....................... kuladuhitā vā puṇyaṃ prasavati / ya ito ratnakūṭaṃ sūtrāntarājñādekagāthām apyupadiśet
body.translated_text: KP.157 Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> said to the Blessed One: How wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>! How wonderful, <s>Sugata</s>! This <s>Mahāratnakūṭa</s> (Great Jewel-Heap) <s>sūtra</s> discourse is [...] extremely beneficial for sons and daughters of good family who have set out upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). How much merit, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does that son [...] or daughter of good family generate who teaches even a single verse from this <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> <s>sūtra</s> discourse?

body.text: KP.158 evamukte bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapam etadavocat - yo hi kāśyapa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā gaṅgānadīvālukasameṣu lokadhā.................... paramāṇuñjāsi bindeya bhitvā tāttakā caiva vārāvāpeya / tāttakā caiva taṃ sarvalokadhātavaḥ sa...................... paripūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ samayaksambuddhebhyo dānaṃ dadyāt / gaṅgānadīvālukasamānāṃ ca buddhā................... bhagavantānām ekekasya ca tathāgatasya gaṅgānadīvālukāsamān vihārān karāpayet /
body.translated_text: KP.158 When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said to the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: If, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a son or daughter of good family were to [...] world-systems equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river [...] reduce them to atoms and scatter them, and gather them again; and having filled all those world-systems, were to give gifts to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly awakened ones; and for <s>Buddhas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river [...] were to have constructed for each <s>Tathāgata</s> monasteries equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river;

body.translated_text: KP.159 And for <s>Buddhas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river [...], were to attend upon the immeasurable <s>Saṅgha</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> of each <s>Tathāgata</s> for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river [...] with comfortable provisions; and were to serve those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, for as long as they live with pleasing conduct of body, speech, and mind [...] in attendance and service; and likewise were to reduce all those world-systems equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river to atoms [...], scatter them, and gather them again; and having filled all those world-systems with the seven precious treasures, were to give gifts to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and for as long as they live with pleasing conduct of body, speech, and mind [...] in attendance and service; and likewise were to honor, revere, respect, and venerate <s>Buddhas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river; and for those who have attained final <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, were to have <s>stūpas</s> made of the seven precious treasures constructed — [even so,] if a son or daughter of good family were to take up even a single verse from this great <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> sūtra, proclaimed by all <s>Buddhas</s> [...] the previous mass of merit would not approach even a hundredth part of this mass of merit, nor a thousandth part [...] nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor any calculation, fraction, enumeration, comparison, or analogy [...]. And whoever should hear [this sūtra] and, having heard it, should not reject it — this [person] would be the producer of an even greater mass of merit. And whoever [...] should hear, or have it written, or master it — for that person there will never be a downfall. That itself will be their [...] final existence.

body.translated_text: KP.160 And whatever region of the earth where this <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma) is spoken, taught, written [...] or where it stands in manuscript form — that region of the earth becomes a shrine for the world including the gods. And in the presence of whatever <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (preacher of the Dharma) [...] one hears, takes up, writes, or masters this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — in the presence of that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>, one should generate reverence [...] just as toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. Whoever [...] will honor, revere, respect, and venerate that preacher [...] at the time of death, there will be a vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.translated_text: KP.161 And through the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one obtains ten purifications of bodily action [...]. What are the ten? Namely: [...] one will die with a mind not overwhelmed by feeling; one's eyes will not be disturbed [...]; one will not make movements of the hands; one will not make movements of the feet; one will not pass excrement; one will not pass urine; [...] one will not perspire; one will not clench the fists; one will not grasp at space; and as one is seated [...]
